name: Basic -c usage: output
script:
# Capture raw output of command
raw_output=$($0 -c 'echo hi')

# Dump raw output as characters
echo "[Character output]"
for ((i = 0; i < ${#raw_output}; i++)); do
  char="${raw_output:i:1}"
  printf '%c' "$char"
done
printf '\n\n'

# Dump raw output as hex
echo "[Hex output]"
for ((i = 0; i < ${#raw_output}; i++)); do
  if (( i % 16 == 0 )); then
    printf '%04x: ' "$i"
  fi

  char="${raw_output:i:1}"
  printf '%02x ' "'$char"

  if (( (i + 1) % 16 == 0 )); then
    printf '\n'
  fi
done

printf '\n'

name: cd ~

mkdir ./my_home
export HOME="$(realpath ./my_home)"
echo "Set HOME: $(basename $HOME)"

  echo "Subshell 1: HOME=$(basename $HOME)"

  echo "pwd: $(basename $PWD)"

mkdir -p ./level1/level2/level3
cd level1
ln -s ./level2/level3 ./symlink

# -L by default
(
  cd ./symlink
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
  cd ..
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
)

name: cd -L
script:
mkdir -p ./level1/level2/level3
cd level1
ln -s ./level2/level3 ./symlink

echo "[Case 1]"
(
  cd ./symlink
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
  cd -L ..
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
)

echo "[Case 2]"
(
  cd -L ./symlink
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
  cd ..
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
)

# without pwd

(
  cd -L ./symlink
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
  export PWD=
  cd -L ..
  echo "$(basename $PWD)"
)

  cd -L ./symlink

)

)

echo "[Case 2]"

name: compgen -A command function in a constrained PATH
compgen -A command with executable symlink
script:
#             pwd
#  drwxr-xr-x ├──  test-bin
# .rwxr-xr-x  │   ├──  dummy_exe
# .rw-r--r--  │   └──  dummy_non_exe
# drwxr-xr-x  └──  test-links
# lrwxrwxrwx      ├──  link_valid         ⇒ $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_exe
# lrwxrwxrwx      └──  link_valid_exe_rec ⇒ $(pwd)/test-links/link_valid
# lrwxrwxrwx      ├──  link_non_exec      ⇒ $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_non_exe
# lrwxrwxrwx      ├──  link_broken        ⇒ $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_non_exist
#
mkdir test-bin
touch test-bin/dummy_exe
touch test-bin/dummy_non_exe
chmod +x test-bin/dummy_exe

mkdir test-links
ln -s $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_exe       $(pwd)/test-links/link_valid
ln -s $(pwd)/test-links/link_vaild    $(pwd)/test-links/link_valid_rec
ln -s $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_non_exe   $(pwd)/test-links/link_non_exec
ln -s $(pwd)/test-bin/dummy_non_exist $(pwd)/test-links/link_broken

PATH="$(pwd)/test-links:$PATH"

echo "[Valid]"
compgen -A command -- link_valid | sort

echo "[Invalid]"
compgen -A command -- link_non_exec
compgen -A command -- link_broken

script:
complete -W x c
for cmd in 'complete -x d' 'complete -A bogus d' 'complete -o bogus d' 'complete -A' \
    'complete -o' 'complete -W' 'complete -W x -A bogus d' 'compopt -x c' \
    'compopt -o bogus c' 'compopt +o bogus c' 'compopt +x c' 'compopt -o' 'compopt +o'; do
  $cmd 2>/dev/null; echo "$cmd: rc=$?"
done
complete -p

name: compopt takes +D, +E, and +I as -D, -E, and -I
script:
complete -D -W x; complete -E -W y; complete -I -W z
compopt +D -o nospace; echo "rc=$?"
compopt +E -o nospace; echo "rc=$?"
compopt +I +o nospace -o dirnames; echo "rc=$?"
for flag in -D -E -I; do complete -p $flag; done

name: Basic getopts
script:
func() {
  echo "Beginning of args"
  while getopts "ab:" option "$@"; do
    case ${option} in
      a) echo "Option a; OPTARG=${OPTARG}";;
      b) echo "Option b; OPTARG=${OPTARG}";;
      *) echo "Unknown option: ${option}";;
    esac
    echo "OPTIND is now ${OPTIND}"
    echo "OPTERR is now ${OPTERR}"
  echo "----------------"
  done
  echo "Result: $?"
  echo "option: ${option}"
  echo "End of args"
}

func -a -b my_b_arg
echo "OPTARG: ${OPTARG}"
echo "OPTIND: ${OPTIND}"

name: hash -p refuses a directory

# Normalize away the leading "shell: line N:" that the oracle prefixes onto diagnostics.
strip() { sed 's/^.*hash:/hash:/'; }

mkdir -p adir
touch afile

echo "[a directory is refused]"
hash -p adir z1 2>&1 | strip; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
# The pipeline above ran in a subshell, so re-run it here to check the table itself.
hash -p adir z1 2>/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
hash -t z1 2>&1 | strip; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

echo "[any other path is taken at face value]"
hash -p afile z2; echo "rc=$?"
hash -p /nonexistent/x z3; echo "rc=$?"
hash -t z2 z3; echo "rc=$?"

echo "[refused once per name]"
hash -p adir bad1 bad2 2>&1 | strip; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

echo "[a relative path resolves against the shell's working directory]"
mkdir -p sub/reldir sub2
cd sub
hash -p reldir z4 2>&1 | strip; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
cd ../sub2
# ../sub/reldir exists, but 'reldir' does not from here, so this is just a path.
hash -p reldir z5 2>/dev/null; echo "rc=$?"
hash -t z5; echo "rc=$?"
cd ..

echo "[hash NAME stays strict about executables]"
mkdir -p d1; touch d1/only
PATH="d1:$PATH"
hash only 2>&1 | strip; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

chmod +x prog
PATH="$PWD:$PATH"

prog

name: Basic async job
script:
echo hi &
wait

name: fg resumes a stopped job without a terminal to give it
script:
set -m
sh -c 'kill -STOP $$; echo resumed'
fg >/dev/null
echo "fg: $?"

name: fg resumes every process of a stopped job
script:
set -m
sh -c '(kill -STOP 0; echo child resumed); echo parent resumed'
fg >/dev/null
echo "fg: $?"

name: bg on a job already in the background says so
script:
set -m
strip() { sed -E 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //'; }
sleep 1 &
bg %1 2>err.txt; echo "bg: $?"; strip < err.txt
wait %1
rm err.txt

name: fg without a current job reports on stderr
script:
fg
echo "fg: $?"

name: fg and bg report a job that doesn't exist on stderr, naming the builtin first
script:
set -m
strip() { sed -E 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //'; }
fg %5 2>err.txt; echo "fg: $?"; strip < err.txt
bg %5 2>err.txt; echo "bg: $?"; strip < err.txt
rm err.txt

name: fg without job control says so
Job builtins fail with status 1 for a job that doesn't exist
script:
jobs %9
echo "jobs: $?"
disown %9
echo "disown: $?"

name: Job builtins check for job control before their options
script:
fg -Z
echo "fg: $?"
bg -Z
echo "bg: $?"
disown -Z
echo "disown: $?"

name: wait returns once a job stops, and the job stays stopped
script:
set -m
sh -c 'kill -STOP $$; echo resumed' &
wait %1; echo "wait: $?"
jobs -s >stopped.txt; echo "stopped: $(( $(wc -l <stopped.txt) ))"
fg >/dev/null; echo "fg: $?"
rm stopped.txt

name: fg notices a job it continued stopping again
script:
set -m
sh -c 'kill -STOP $$; kill -STOP $$; echo resumed' &
wait %1; echo "wait: $?"
fg >/dev/null; echo "fg: $?"
fg >/dev/null; echo "fg: $?"

name: set -m gives a job a process group of its own
script: set -m; sh -c 'read -r _ _ _ _ pgid _ < /proc/$$/stat; [ "$pgid" -eq $$ ] && echo own-group'

name: wait for every job reports none of them
script:
set -m
true &
wait
echo done

name: wait for a job that's stopped returns at once
script:
set -m
sh -c 'kill -STOP $$; echo resumed' &
wait %1; echo "first: $?"
wait %1; echo "again: $?"
kill -9 %1

name: wait for every job leaves out the stopped ones
script:
set -m
sh -c 'kill -STOP $$; echo resumed' &
wait %1
sleep 0.1 &
wait >/dev/null; echo "all: $?"
jobs -s >stopped.txt; echo "stopped: $(( $(wc -l <stopped.txt) ))"
kill -9 %1
rm stopped.txt

name: jobs in a pipeline lists the shell's jobs
script:
sleep 0.3 &
jobs | wc -l
wait

name: kill -l
script:
for i in $(seq 1 31); do kill -l $i; done
# limit the number of signals to 31. Realtime signals are not implemented yet.
for i in $(kill -l | sed -e "s/[[:digit:]]*)//g"); do echo $i; done | head -31
# invalid option
kill -l 9999
kill -l HUP
kill -l iNt
kill -l int
kill -l SIGHUP
kill -l EXIT

name: kill continues a stopped job sent SIGTERM, so it can act on it
script:
set -m
sh -c 'trap "echo terminated >status.txt; exit 3" TERM; kill -STOP $$; echo resumed'
kill -TERM %1
for i in $(seq 100); do [ -s status.txt ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
cat status.txt
rm -f status.txt

name: kill continues a job sent SIGTERM that stopped again in the background
script:
set -m
sh -c 'echo $$ >pid.txt; trap "echo terminated >status.txt; exit 3" TERM; kill -STOP $$; kill -STOP $$'
bg >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 100); do case $(ps -o stat= -p "$(cat pid.txt)") in T*) break ;; esac; sleep 0.1; done
kill -TERM %1
for i in $(seq 100); do [ -s status.txt ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
cat status.txt
rm -f pid.txt status.txt

name: A stopped job that survives SIGTERM runs on
script:
set -m
sh -c 'trap "echo caught >status.txt" TERM; kill -STOP $$; while [ ! -e done.txt ]; do sleep 0.1; done'
kill -TERM %1
for i in $(seq 100); do [ -s status.txt ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
cat status.txt
jobs -r >running.txt; echo "running: $(( $(wc -l <running.txt) ))"
jobs -s >stopped.txt; echo "stopped: $(( $(wc -l <stopped.txt) ))"
touch done.txt
wait %1
rm -f status.txt done.txt running.txt stopped.txt

name: kill sends SIGTERM by default
script:
sh -c 'trap "echo got TERM; exit 0" TERM; echo $$ > pidfile; while :; do sleep 0.05; done' &
while [ ! -s pidfile ]; do sleep 0.05; done
kill "$(cat pidfile)"
wait
# The process ID differs from run to run.
rm pidfile

name: kill takes -- before a process group, and -s 0
script:
kill -0 -- $$; echo "a=$?"
kill -s 0 $$; echo "b=$?"
kill -0 -- -$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' '); echo "c=$?"
# An exited process's ID names no process or group, so nothing else is signaled.
dead=$(sh -c 'echo $$')
kill -- -$dead; echo "d=$?"
kill -s TERM -- -$dead; echo "e=$?"

name: kill takes -N after a signal as a process group
script:
# Signal 0 checks this shell's own group without signaling it.
kill -0 -$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ | tr -d ' '); echo "a=$?"
# An exited process's ID names no process or group, so nothing else is
# signaled; only the reason kill gives for failing is compared.
dead=$(sh -c 'echo $$')
kill -TERM -$dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "b=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

name: kill takes -N alone as a signal number
script:
# -999999 is an invalid signal number here, not a target.
kill -999999 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

name: kill takes the words after its first operand as operands

kill -0 $$ -l || true

name: kill takes its signal in each form
script:
kill -l -- 9
kill -l HUP
# An exited process's ID names no process or group, so nothing else is
# signaled; only the reason kill gives for failing is compared.
dead=$(sh -c 'echo $$')
kill -sUSR1 $dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "a=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
kill -n9 $dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "b=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
kill -HUP $dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "c=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

name: kill takes options after a -SIG shorthand

name: kill takes -- after a signal

# signaled; only the reason kill gives for failing is compared.
dead=$(sh -c 'echo $$')
kill -9 -- $dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "a=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
kill -s HUP -- -$dead 2>&1 | grep -c 'invalid signal'; echo "b=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

name: mapfile checks every count, origin and descriptor it is given
script:
# Only whether it fails is compared: the status itself is a known failure.
exec 99<&-  # fd 99 must be closed, but the harness can leak one in
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -s-1 -s0 arr <<< data; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -c0 -c5000 arr <<< data; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -n-1 -n1 arr <<< data; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -O-1 -O0 arr <<< data; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -u 99 -u 0 arr <<< data; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"
arr=(keep); mapfile -t -s0 -s1 arr <<< $'a\nb'; echo "failed=$(($? != 0)) ${arr[*]}"

name: printf -v with no format fails

name: printf -v with an invalid name fails with status 2
script:

printf -v -- '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"
printf -v-x '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"
printf -v 'a b' '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"
printf -v '' '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"
printf -v 'a[' '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"
printf -v 'a[]' '%s' x; echo "rc=$?"

name: printf -v rejects a subscript with text after its closing bracket

declare -p a 2>/dev/null || echo "a unset"
printf -v 'a[x[1]]' '%s' x; echo "nested: rc=$?"
declare -A m; printf -v 'm["]"]' '%s' x; echo "quoted: rc=$? ${m["]"]}"

name: printf -v checks every name it is given
script:

x=old; printf -v 1bad -v x '%s' new; echo "rc=$? x=$x"
x=old; printf -v x -v 1bad '%s' new; echo "rc=$? x=$x"
printf -v y -v x '%s' last; echo "rc=$? x=$x y=${y-unset}"

x=old; printf -v 'a["x]' -v x '%s' new; echo "rc=$? x=$x"

x=old; printf -v 'a[[]' -v x '%s' new; echo "rc=$? x=$x"

name: printf -v takes a[@] and a[*] as names but can't assign to them

x=old; printf -v 'a[*]' -v x '%s' new; echo "rc=$? x=$x"
printf -v 'a[@]' '%s' v; echo "rc=$? ${a[*]-unset}"
printf -v 'a[*]' '%s' v; echo "rc=$? ${a[*]-unset}"

name: printf --help prints help on stdout

name: read -n counts output chars after escape processing
script:
# Bash counts OUTPUT characters toward -n limit (after escape processing).
# Input: a, \, b, c = 4 input bytes. With -n 3:
# 'a' (output 1), '\b' → 'b' (output 2), 'c' (output 3) = "abc"
printf 'a\\bc' | { read -n 3 var; echo "var='$var'"; }
# Input: \, \, a, b = 4 input bytes. With -n 3:
# '\\' → '\' (output 1), 'a' (output 2), 'b' (output 3) = "\ab"
printf '\\\\ab' | { read -n 3 var; echo "var='$var'"; }

name: read -n with backslash-newline continuation
script:
# Backslash-newline is line continuation (consumes both, outputs nothing).
# Input: a, b, \, \n, c = 5 input bytes. With -n 3:
# 'a' (output 1), 'b' (output 2), '\n' → continuation, 'c' (output 3) = "abc"
printf 'ab\\\nc' | { read -n 3 var; echo "var='$var'"; }

name: read -h is an invalid option and prints nothing on stdout
script: x=$(read -h 2>/dev/null); echo "rc=$? len=${#x}"

name: making var readonly
script:
my_var="value"
readonly my_var

echo "Invoking declare -p..."
declare -p my_var

name: using readonly with value
script:
readonly my_var="my_value"

echo "Invoking declare -p..."
declare -p my_var

name: readonly array after append
script:
ARR=()
f() {
    ARR+=("a" "b")
    readonly ARR
    echo "${#ARR[@]}"
}
f

name: Multiple readonly operands expand before assignments are applied
script:
unset first second
readonly first=one second=$first
declare -p first second

name: readonly on nameref makes nameref readonly
script:
target="value"
declare -n ref=target
readonly ref
declare -p ref
declare -p target
# Changing what ref points to should fail
declare -n ref=other 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
# But target should still be writable
target="new_value"
echo "target: $target"

name: readonly target through nameref assignment
script:
target="value"
readonly target
declare -n ref=target
ref="new_value" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "target: $target"

name: readonly -f marks a function readonly rather than displaying it
Return outside function or script
script: return 42

name: Return outside function with stderr to /dev/full
script:
# /dev/full may not be available on all platforms.
[[ -e /dev/full ]] || exit 0
return 2>/dev/full
echo "exit: $?"

name: Return from sourced script
script: source script.sh

name: Return from subshell
script:
(return)
echo "Got past subshell"
exit 42

name: Return from nested sourced script
script: source outer.sh

name: Return in for loop in function
script:
myfunc() {
    for i in 1 2 3; do
        echo "In myfunc: $i"
        return 5
    done
}

myfunc
echo "Returned: $?"

name: Return in arithmetic for loop in function
script:
myfunc() {
    for ((i=0; i < 5; i++)); do
        echo "In myfunc: $i"
        return 5
    done
}

myfunc
echo "Returned: $?"

name: Return in while loop in function
script:
myfunc() {
    i=0
    while [[ $i -lt 5 ]]; do
      echo "In myfunc: $i"
      return 33
      i=$((i+1))
    done
}

myfunc
echo "Returned: $?"

name: Return in case
script:
myfunc() {
  case 1 in
      1)
          echo "In case"
          return 5
          echo "Should not get here"
          ;;
  esac
}

myfunc
echo "Returned: $?"

name: Return in brace group
Return in and/or
Return from nested clauses
return with a non-numeric argument returns 2
return with too many arguments abandons the rest of the line
return takes -- and a negative status
script:
f() { return -1; }; f; echo "a=$?"
f() { return -256; }; f; echo "b=$?"
f() { return -0; }; false; f; echo "c=$?"
f() { return -- 6; }; f; echo "d=$?"

name: set with no args
script:
MYVARIABLE=VALUE
set > set-output.txt
grep MYVARIABLE set-output.txt

# Remove set-output.txt to avoid it being byte-for-byte compared.
rm set-output.txt

name: Basic set usage
script:
set a b c d
echo ${*}

name: set with options
script:
function dumpopts {
    # Dump the options
    echo "[Options: $1]"
    echo "set options: " $-
    shopt -p -o pipefail
}

set -e -u -o pipefail
dumpopts enabled
echo '*: ' $*

set +e +u +o pipefail
dumpopts disabled
echo '*: ' $*

name: set with multiple combined options
script:
function dumpopts {
    # Dump the options
    echo "[Options: $1]"
    echo "set options: " $-
    shopt -p -o pipefail
}

set -euo pipefail
dumpopts enabled
echo '$*: ' $*

set +euo pipefail
dumpopts disabled
echo '$*: ' $*

name: set clearing args
set with -
set with --
set with option-looking args
function-local set
script:
function f() {
    local -
    set -x
    echo "In func"
}

echo "Before func"
f
echo "After func"

name: set output quotes values
script:
q1="a'b"; q2="a''b"; q3="'"; q4="''"; q5="'a"; q6="a'"
set > set-output.txt
grep -E '^q[0-9]=' set-output.txt

# Remove set-output.txt to avoid it being byte-for-byte compared.
rm set-output.txt

name: set output leaves an empty value unquoted
script:
q1=""
set > set-output.txt
grep -E '^q[0-9]=' set-output.txt

# Remove set-output.txt to avoid it being byte-for-byte compared.
rm set-output.txt

name: set quotes values starting with # or ~
script:
x="~" y="#z" z="a=~" w="a~"
set | grep -E "^(w|x|y|z)="

name: set leaves commas unquoted, like bash
script:
x="a,b" y="{a,b}" z=","
set | grep -E "^(x|y|z)="

name: set and declare -p leave commas in associative array keys unquoted, like bash
script:
declare -A m=([a,b]=1 [c]=2)
set | grep "^m="
declare -p m

name: set applies -o and +o in the order given
script:
set -o noglob +o noglob; echo "1 $-"
set +o noglob -o noglob; echo "2 $-"; set +f
set -o noglob -o noclobber +o noglob; echo "3 $-"; set +fC

name: set applies letters and -o names in the order given
script:
set -f +o noglob; echo "1 $-"
set -o noglob +f; echo "2 $-"; set +f
set +o noglob -f; echo "3 $-"; set +f
set -eo pipefail +e; echo "4 $-"; shopt -po pipefail; set +o pipefail

name: set -o alone after a name lists the options it just set
script:
set -o noglob -o | grep noglob
set +o noglob +o | grep noglob

name: set stops at an unknown option name
script:
set -- q
set -o nosuch -f a b; echo "$? $- [$*]"

name: set - turns off -x and -v
script:
set -x -v; set -; echo "1 $-"
set -x; set -e -; echo "2 $-"; set +e
set -x -v; set -- a; set +xv; echo "3 $- [$*]"

name: set -o with an unknown option name
script:
strip() { sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g; s/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //; s/^error: //'; }
set -o bogus 2>&1 | strip
echo "set -o: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
set +o bogus 2>&1 | strip
echo "set +o: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

name: set takes the letters after -o as more options
script:
set -oe | tail -1
set -oe >/dev/null; echo "$-"
set +oe | tail -1
set +oe >/dev/null; echo "$-"

name: set rejects an option it doesn't have
script:
set -Z; echo "set -Z: $?"
set +Z; echo "set +Z: $?"

name: set accepts -r and +r
script:
set +r; echo "+r: $?"
set -r; echo "-r: $?"

name: set -r turns on restricted mode
script:
set -r; echo "status: $?"
[[ $- == *r* ]] && echo "restricted"
cd / 2>/dev/null; echo "cd: $?"

name: set skips a lone +
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set a b; set +; echo "$# $*"
set + | wc -l
set + x y; echo "$# $*"
set + -e; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
set -e + z; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
set + + -u; opts; set +u
set + -- w; echo "$# $*"
set -- +; echo "$# $*"
set - +; echo "$# $*"
set v + -e; opts; echo "$# $*"

name: set rejects an unknown letter after a lone + with status 1
script: set + -Z; echo "status: $?"

name: set applies the options before a lone + when a later one is unknown
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -f + -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +f
set -f -u + -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +fu
set a b; set -f + -Z c; echo "status: $?"; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +f
# Without a lone +, an unknown letter stops set before any option applies.
set -f -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts

name: set applies the options after a lone + up to an unknown one
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set + -u -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +u
set + -uZ; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +u
set + -Zu; echo "status: $?"; opts

name: set -o and +o list the options as they stand at that point
script:
set -eo | grep '^errexit'
set -oe | grep '^errexit'
set -o errexit -o | grep '^errexit'
set -o -o errexit | grep '^errexit'
set +o -e | grep ' errexit$'
set -e +o | grep ' errexit$'
set -u -o -u | grep '^nounset'
set -o '' | grep '^errexit'
set +o '' | grep ' errexit$'
set +o -o | grep -E '^(set [-+]o errexit|errexit)'

name: set -o takes an empty word as its first operand
script:
set a; set -o '' -e >/dev/null; echo "$- $# [$*]"
set -o '' x >/dev/null; echo "$# [$*]"

name: set applies -x and +x in command-line order
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -e +e; opts
set +e -e; opts; set +e
set -u +eu -e; opts; set +e
set -eux +eux; opts
set -e -e +e +e -e; opts; set +e
set -B +B; opts; set +B -B; opts
set -C +C -C; opts; set +C
: > zzglob; set -f +f; echo zzg*; set +f -f; echo zzg*; set +f
set -e +u; opts; set +e

name: set applies -o and +o in order with the letter options
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -o errexit +e; opts
set +e -o errexit; opts; set +e
# shopt -po fails for an option that is off; || keeps errexit from ending the case.
set -eo pipefail +o pipefail; opts; shopt -po pipefail || :; set +e
set +o pipefail -o pipefail +o pipefail; shopt -po pipefail
set -o pipefail +o pipefail -o pipefail; shopt -po pipefail; set +o pipefail
set -o nounset -o errexit +o nounset; opts; set +e
set +o errexit +o nounset -eu; opts; set +eu
set -a -o allexport +a; opts
set -uo nounset +u; opts
set -x +o xtrace; opts

name: set -o or +o with no name, then more options or operands
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -o -e >/dev/null; opts; set +e
set +o -u >/dev/null; opts; set +u
set -oe >/dev/null; opts; set +e
set -o -- a b >/dev/null; echo "$# $*"
set -o >/dev/null -- c; echo "$# $*"

name: set stops at an unknown option name among other options and operands
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -o nosuch -u 2>/dev/null; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -u -o nosuch 2>/dev/null; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +u
# set fails here with errexit on; || keeps it from ending the case.
set -o errexit +o nosuch -o nounset 2>/dev/null || echo "status: $?"; opts; set +e
set a b; set -o nosuch c d 2>/dev/null; echo "$# $*"
set -o nosuch -- e f 2>/dev/null; echo "$# $*"
set -o nosuch -o 2>/dev/null; echo "listed nothing"

name: set rejects an unknown letter before applying any option
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -e -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -eZ; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -Ze -u; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -o errexit -Z; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -o -Z | head -1; opts
set -ex+u; echo "status: $?"; opts
set a b; set -Z c; echo "$# $*"

name: set - turns off -x and -v and ends the options
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in v x; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
{ set -x; set -; } 2>/dev/null; opts
{ set -xv; set - a; } 2>/dev/null; opts; echo "$# $*"
{ set -x -e - b; } 2>/dev/null; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
{ set -x - -e; } 2>/dev/null; opts; echo "$# $*"
{ set -x - -; } 2>/dev/null; opts; echo "$# $*"

name: set takes options only before its operands
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -- -x; opts; echo "$# $*"
set x -e; opts; echo "$# $*"
set -e a -u; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
set -e -- -a; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
set -o errexit x -o nounset; opts; echo "$# $*"; set +e
set +o errexit nosuch; echo "status: $?"; echo "$# $*"
set - -Z; echo "$# $*"
set -- -- a; echo "$# $*"
set - -- a; echo "$# $*"
set -- - a; echo "$# $*"
set x -- y; echo "$# $*"
set x - y; echo "$# $*"
set ''; echo "$#"
set -e ''; opts; echo "$#"; set +e

name: set leaves the positional parameters alone without operands
script:
set a b c
set -e; echo "$#"; set +e
set -o errexit; echo "$#"; set +e
set -o >/dev/null; echo "$#"
set +o >/dev/null; echo "$#"
set -; echo "$#"
set -e -; echo "$#"; set +e
set --; echo "$#"

name: set -o in the middle of a bundle takes the next word
set -o takes no name that starts with + or is a lone - or +
script:
opts() { local o r=; for o in a e f u x B C; do case $- in *"$o"*) r+=$o ;; esac; done; echo "[$r]"; }
set -e; set -o +e >/dev/null; echo "status: $?"; opts
set -o - >/dev/null; echo "status: $?"
set -o + a >/dev/null; echo "status: $?"; echo "$# $*"
set +o +o errexit >/dev/null; echo "status: $?"; opts; set +e

name: set -o vi and -o emacs turn each other off
script:
set -o vi -o emacs; set -o | grep -E '^(vi|emacs) '
set -o emacs -o vi; set -o | grep -E '^(vi|emacs) '

name: shift past the end fails with status 1
script:
set -- a
shift 2
echo "shift: $?"

name: A non-numeric shift count is misuse, in bash's words
script:
strip() { sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g; s/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]+: //; s/^error: //'; }
set -- a b
shift x 2>err.txt
echo "shift x: $?"
strip <err.txt
rm err.txt

name: shift with a negative count reports it and fails with status 1
script:
set -- a b
shift -1 2>err.txt; echo "shift -1: $? $#"
[[ -s err.txt ]] && echo "reported"
shift -0; echo "shift -0: $? $#"
rm err.txt

name: shift takes --
script:
set -- a b c
shift -- 2; echo "$? $*"

name: shift with too many arguments abandons the rest of the line
script:
set -- a b
shift 1 2; echo "same line: $?"
echo "next line: $? $#"

name: shopt defaults
script: shopt | sort | grep -v extglob

name: shopt -o defaults
script: shopt -o | sort

name: extglob defaults
script: shopt extglob

name: shopt toggle
script:
echo "Setting checkwinsize"
shopt -s checkwinsize

echo "Displaying checkwinsize"
shopt checkwinsize
shopt -p checkwinsize

echo "Unsetting checkwinsize"
shopt -u checkwinsize

echo "Displaying checkwinsize"
shopt checkwinsize
shopt -p checkwinsize

name: shopt -o usage
script:
echo "Setting emacs"
shopt -o -s emacs

echo "Displaying emacs"
shopt -o emacs
shopt -o -p emacs

echo "Unsetting emacs"
shopt -o -u emacs

echo "Displaying emacs"
shopt -o emacs
shopt -o -p emacs

name: shopt refuses to set and unset at once
shopt takes -- and -o with -s, -u, -p and -q
script:
shopt -s -- nullglob; shopt -p nullglob
shopt -so errexit; [[ $- == *e* ]] && echo "errexit on"
shopt -po errexit
shopt -uo errexit; shopt -qo errexit; echo "q=$?"

name: suspend without job control fails
script:
suspend
echo "suspend: $?"

name: suspend with an operand abandons the rest of the line
script:
suspend foo; echo "same line: $?"
echo "next line: $?"

name: test: = operator
script:
shopt -u nocasematch
test "ab" = "ab" && echo "ab = ab"
test "ab" = "AB" && echo "ab = AB"
test "ab" = "cd" && echo "ab = cd"
test "ab" = "a?" && echo "ab = a?"

shopt -s nocasematch
test "ab" = "ab" && echo "ab = ab"
test "ab" = "AB" && echo "ab = AB"
test "ab" = "cd" && echo "ab = cd"
test "ab" = "a?" && echo "ab = a?"

name: test: == operator
script:
shopt -u nocasematch
test "ab" == "ab" && echo "ab == ab"
test "ab" == "AB" && echo "ab == AB"
test "ab" == "cd" && echo "ab == cd"
test "ab" == "a?" && echo "ab == a?"

shopt -s nocasematch
test "ab" == "ab" && echo "ab == ab"
test "ab" == "AB" && echo "ab == AB"
test "ab" == "cd" && echo "ab == cd"
test "ab" == "a?" && echo "ab == a?"

name: test: files refer to same device and inode
script:
[ /bin/sh -ef /bin/sh ] && echo "-ef correctly identified device and inode numbers"

[ ! /etc/os-release -ef /bin/sh ] && echo "-ef correctly identified device and inode numbers that do not match"

name: test: file is newer
script:
touch -d "2 hours ago" bar
touch foo

[ foo -nt bar ] && echo "-nt correctly identified newer file"
[ foo -nt foo ] && echo "-nt incorrectly identified file as newer than itself"
[ foo -nt file_no_exists ] && echo "-nt correctly identified when file2 does not exist"

name: test: file is older
script:
touch -d "2 hours ago" foo
touch bar

[ foo -ot bar ] && echo "-ot correctly identified older file"
[ foo -ot foo ] && echo "-ot incorrectly identified file as older than itself"
[ file_no_exists -ot foo ] && echo "-ot correctly identified when file1 does not exist"

name: test: parens
script: test \( "a" = "a" \) && echo "Parens work"

name: test: -- string
script:
test --
echo "Result(test): $?"

[ -- ]
echo "Result([): $?"

name: test: invalid operators
script:
test - -
echo "Result: $?"

name: test: != operator
script:
test "ab" != "cd" && echo "ab != cd"
test "ab" != "ab" && echo "ab != ab"
test "" != "x" && echo "empty != x"

name: test: -z operator (zero length)
script:
test -z "" && echo "-z empty"
test -z "x" && echo "-z x"
unset VAR
test -z "$VAR" && echo "-z unset"

name: test: -n operator (non-zero length)
script:
test -n "x" && echo "-n x"
test -n "" && echo "-n empty"
VAR="hello"
test -n "$VAR" && echo "-n set"

name: test: < operator (string sort before)
script:
test "a" \< "b" && echo "a < b"
test "b" \< "a" && echo "b < a"
test "abc" \< "abd" && echo "abc < abd"
test "a" \< "a" && echo "a < a"

name: test: > operator (string sort after)
script:
test "b" \> "a" && echo "b > a"
test "a" \> "b" && echo "a > b"
test "abd" \> "abc" && echo "abd > abc"
test "a" \> "a" && echo "a > a"

name: test: -eq operator
script:
test 5 -eq 5 && echo "5 -eq 5"
test 5 -eq 6 && echo "5 -eq 6"
test -1 -eq -1 && echo "-1 -eq -1"
test 0 -eq 0 && echo "0 -eq 0"

name: test: -ne operator
script:
test 5 -ne 6 && echo "5 -ne 6"
test 5 -ne 5 && echo "5 -ne 5"
test -1 -ne 1 && echo "-1 -ne 1"

name: test: -lt operator
script:
test 3 -lt 5 && echo "3 -lt 5"
test 5 -lt 3 && echo "5 -lt 3"
test 5 -lt 5 && echo "5 -lt 5"
test -2 -lt -1 && echo "-2 -lt -1"

name: test: -le operator
script:
test 3 -le 5 && echo "3 -le 5"
test 5 -le 5 && echo "5 -le 5"
test 6 -le 5 && echo "6 -le 5"
test -2 -le -2 && echo "-2 -le -2"

name: test: -gt operator
script:
test 5 -gt 3 && echo "5 -gt 3"
test 3 -gt 5 && echo "3 -gt 5"
test 5 -gt 5 && echo "5 -gt 5"
test -1 -gt -2 && echo "-1 -gt -2"

name: test: -ge operator
script:
test 5 -ge 3 && echo "5 -ge 3"
test 5 -ge 5 && echo "5 -ge 5"
test 3 -ge 5 && echo "3 -ge 5"
test -1 -ge -1 && echo "-1 -ge -1"

name: test: -e operator (file exists)
script:
touch testfile
test -e testfile && echo "-e existing file"
test -e nonexistent && echo "-e nonexistent"
mkdir testdir
test -e testdir && echo "-e existing dir"

name: test: -a operator (file exists, deprecated)
script:
touch testfile
test -a testfile && echo "-a existing file"
test -a nonexistent && echo "-a nonexistent"

name: test: -f operator (regular file)
script:
touch testfile
test -f testfile && echo "-f regular file"
mkdir testdir
test -f testdir && echo "-f directory"
test -f nonexistent && echo "-f nonexistent"

name: test: -d operator (directory)
script:
mkdir testdir
test -d testdir && echo "-d directory"
touch testfile
test -d testfile && echo "-d regular file"
test -d nonexistent && echo "-d nonexistent"

name: test: -h and -L operators (symbolic link)
script:
touch target
ln -s target symlink
test -h symlink && echo "-h symlink"
test -L symlink && echo "-L symlink"
test -h target && echo "-h regular file"
test -L target && echo "-L regular file"
test -h nonexistent && echo "-h nonexistent"

name: test: -p operator (named pipe/FIFO)
script:
touch testfile
test -p testfile && echo "-p regular file"
test -p nonexistent && echo "-p nonexistent"

name: test: -S operator (socket)
script:
touch testfile
test -S testfile && echo "-S regular file"
test -S nonexistent && echo "-S nonexistent"

name: test: -b operator (block device)
script:
touch testfile
test -b testfile && echo "-b regular file"
test -b nonexistent && echo "-b nonexistent"
# Block devices exist in /dev but may vary by system

name: test: -c operator (character device)
script:
touch testfile
test -c testfile && echo "-c regular file"
test -c nonexistent && echo "-c nonexistent"

name: test: -r operator (readable)
script:
touch testfile
test -r testfile && echo "-r readable"
test -r nonexistent && echo "-r nonexistent"

name: test: -w operator (writable)
script:
touch testfile
test -w testfile && echo "-w writable"
test -w nonexistent && echo "-w nonexistent"

name: test: -x operator (executable)
script:
touch testfile
test -x testfile && echo "-x executable"

name: test: -s operator (size greater than zero)
script:
echo "content" > nonempty
test -s nonempty && echo "-s nonempty"
touch empty
test -s empty && echo "-s empty"
test -s nonexistent && echo "-s nonexistent"

name: test: -v operator (variable is set)
script:
VAR="hello"
test -v VAR && echo "-v set variable"
unset VAR
test -v VAR && echo "-v unset variable"
VAR=""
test -v VAR && echo "-v empty variable"

name: test: -R operator (nameref variable)
script:
VAR="value"
declare -n REF=VAR
test -R REF && echo "-R nameref"
test -R VAR && echo "-R regular var"
unset REF VAR

name: test: -o operator (shell option)
script:
set -e
test -o errexit && echo "-o errexit enabled"
set +e
test -o errexit && echo "-o errexit disabled"
test -o nonexistentoption && echo "-o nonexistent"

name: test: ! operator (negation)
script:
test ! "a" = "b" && echo "! a=b"
test ! "a" = "a" && echo "! a=a"
test ! -e nonexistent && echo "! -e nonexistent"
test ! -e / && echo "! -e /"

name: test: -a operator (logical AND)
script:
test "a" = "a" -a "b" = "b" && echo "true -a true"
test "a" = "a" -a "b" = "c" && echo "true -a false"
test "a" = "b" -a "c" = "c" && echo "false -a true"
test "a" = "b" -a "c" = "d" && echo "false -a false"

name: test: -o operator (logical OR)
script:
test "a" = "a" -o "b" = "b" && echo "true -o true"
test "a" = "a" -o "b" = "c" && echo "true -o false"
test "a" = "b" -o "c" = "c" && echo "false -o true"
test "a" = "b" -o "c" = "d" && echo "false -o false"

name: test: complex logical expressions
script:
test \( "a" = "a" -o "b" = "c" \) -a "d" = "d" && echo "complex 1"
test ! \( "a" = "b" \) && echo "complex 2"
test "a" = "a" -a \( "b" = "b" -o "c" = "d" \) && echo "complex 3"

name: test: single argument (non-empty string is true)
script:
test "hello" && echo "non-empty is true"
test "" && echo "empty is true"
test "0" && echo "zero string is true"

name: test: no arguments
script:
test
echo "no args: $?"

name: test: special characters in strings
script:
test "hello world" = "hello world" && echo "spaces match"
test "a	b" = "a	b" && echo "tabs match"
test 'a"b' = 'a"b' && echo "quotes match"
test "a'b" = "a'b" && echo "single quotes match"

name: test: arithmetic comparison with spaces/tabs in operand
script:
# Leading/trailing spaces
test 0 -eq ' 0'
echo "leading space: $?"

test 0 -eq '0 '
echo "trailing space: $?"

test 0 -eq ' 0 '
echo "both spaces: $?"

# Tabs
test 0 -eq '	0'
echo "leading tab: $?"

test 0 -eq '0	'
echo "trailing tab: $?"

name: test: arithmetic comparison with newline in operand

'

name: test: -t operator with whitespace in fd

# These should all behave identically (false since not a terminal)
test -t 0
r1=$?
test -t ' 0'
r2=$?
test -t '0 '
r3=$?
test -t ' 0 '
r4=$?

# All should have the same result
[ $r1 -eq $r2 ] && [ $r2 -eq $r3 ] && [ $r3 -eq $r4 ] && echo "All -t results match"

echo "[: $?"

test --help; echo "d=$?"
test -h; echo "e=$?"

name: Single-line for loop

name: Multi-line for loop

    true && break

    break 2
  done

name: Continue in for loop

  continue
  echo $f
done

name: Continue with bad N

  continue 0
  echo result: $?
done

name: Continue in nested for loop

  for g in 1 2 3; do
    echo "f=$f g=$g"
    continue
    echo "Should not print"
  done
  echo "Left inner loop"
done

name: Continue in nested for loop with explicit N=1

name: break and continue with a count of zero leave every loop

echo "after break: $?"
for i in 1 2; do for j in a b; do continue -1; done; echo "outer $i"; done
echo "after continue: $?"

name: break and continue outside a loop

break; echo "after break: $?"
continue; echo "after continue: $?"

name: break and continue check for a loop before their options

f

name: break and continue act only on the loops of the current function
break and continue in a substitution act on the enclosing loops
script:
for i in 1 2; do x=$(break; echo "not captured"); echo "captured [$x]"; done
for i in 1; do x=$(for j in 1; do break 2; done; echo "not captured"); echo "[$x]"; done
for i in 1; do cat <(break; echo "not read"); echo "after process substitution"; done

name: break and continue past the outermost loop
script:
for i in 1 2; do for j in a b; do break 5; done; echo "not reached"; done
echo "after break: $?"
for i in 1 2; do for j in a b; do echo "$i$j"; continue 9; done; done
echo "after continue: $?"

name: break and continue read their operand as bash does
script:
for i in 1 2; do break -- 1; echo "not reached"; done
echo "after --: $?"
for i in 1 2; do break " 1 "; echo "not reached"; done
echo "after blanks: $?"
for i in 1; do break --help >/dev/null; echo "help: $?"; done

name: break and continue clamp their count to the loop depth
script:
for i in 1 2; do
  for j in 1 2; do break 99; echo "inner $i$j"; done
  echo "outer $i"
done
echo "after: $?"
f() { for k in 1 2; do continue 99; echo "in f $k"; done; echo "f end"; }
for i in 1 2; do f; echo "loop $i"; done

name: break and continue report a negative count and fail with status 1
script:
for i in 1; do break -1 2>err.txt; done; echo "break -1: $?"
[[ -s err.txt ]] && echo "break reported"
for i in 1; do continue -1 2>err.txt; done; echo "continue -1: $?"
[[ -s err.txt ]] && echo "continue reported"
rm err.txt

(set -o bogus; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: set -o bogus"
(set --bogus; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: set --bogus"
(trap -Z; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: trap -Z"
(shift abc; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: shift abc"
(readonly 1x; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: readonly 1x"
(export 1x=2 y=3; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: export 1x=2 y=3"
(readonly r=1; readonly r=2; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: readonly r=1; readonly r=2"
(readonly r=1; unset r; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: readonly r=1; unset r"
(readonly r=1; export r=2; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: readonly r=1; export r=2"
(. /nonexistent-file; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: . /nonexistent-file"
(f() { return abc; }; f; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: f() { return abc; }; f"
(return 3; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: return 3"
(exec -Z; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: exec -Z"
(export --help >/dev/null; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: export --help >/dev/null"
(for i in 1; do break abc; done; echo "survived: $?")
echo "status $?: for i in 1; do break abc; done"

name: A special builtin's ordinary failures are not fatal in POSIX mode
script:
set -o posix
for cmd in 'trap x BOGUS' 'set -- a; shift 3' 'export -f nofunc' 'unset -f -v x' \
    'unset 1x' 'for i in 1; do break 0; done' 'break' 'continue 2'; do
  (eval "$cmd"; echo "survived $?: $cmd")
done

name: A failed exec ends a non-interactive shell unless execfail is set

echo "missing: $?"

echo "not executable: $?"
(shopt -s execfail; exec /nonexistent-command; echo "survived execfail: $?")

(unset HOME; cd) 2>&1 | strip

name: An assignment error drops the rest of the line
script:
readonly r=1
r=2; echo "same line: $?"
echo "next line: $?"
f() { r=3; }; f; echo "same line after f: $?"
echo "next line after f: $?"

name: An error in a redirected group drops the rest of the line
script:
readonly r=1
{ r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after assignment: $?"
echo "next line: $?"
{ echo $((1/0)); } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after arithmetic: $?"
echo "next line: $?"
shopt -s failglob
{ echo /no-such-dir-*; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after failglob: $?"
echo "next line: $?"

name: An error in a redirected compound command drops the rest of the line
script:
readonly r=1
if true; then r=2; fi 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after if: $?"
echo "next line: $?"
for i in 1; do r=2; done 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after for: $?"
echo "next line: $?"
while true; do r=2; done 2>/dev/null; echo "same line after while: $?"
echo "next line: $?"

name: An error in a redirected group isn't a failure for ||
script:
readonly r=1
{ r=2; } 2>/dev/null || echo "ran ||"; echo "same line"
echo "next line"

name: An error in a redirected group isn't a false condition
script:
readonly r=1
if { r=2; } 2>/dev/null; then echo "then"; else echo "else"; fi; echo "same line after if"
echo "next line"
! { r=2; } 2>/dev/null && echo "negated"; echo "same line after !"
echo "next line"

name: An error in a redirected group abandons the enclosing loop
script:
readonly r=1
for i in 1 2 3; do { r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "iteration $i"; done
echo "after for"
i=0
until { r=2; } 2>/dev/null; do i=$((i + 1)); [ $i -ge 3 ] && break; echo "tick $i"; done
echo "after until"
i=0
while true; do { r=2; } 2>/dev/null || break; i=$((i + 1)); [ $i -ge 3 ] && break; done; echo "same line after while"
echo "after while"

name: An error in a redirected group abandons the function it's in
script:
readonly r=1
f() { { r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "still in f"; }
f
echo "next line"

name: An error in a redirected group doesn't run the ERR trap
script:
trap 'echo "ERR trap"' ERR
readonly r=1
{ r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line"
echo "next line"

name: An error in a redirected group drops the rest of the line (POSIX mode)
script:
set -o posix
readonly r=1
{ r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line"

name: A fatal error in a redirected group drops the rest of the line (interactive)
script:
unset zz
{ echo "${zz?missing parameter}"; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line"
echo "next line"

name: An error in a redirected group drops the rest of the line (interactive)
script:
readonly r=1
{ r=2; } 2>/dev/null; echo "same line"
echo "next line"

name: A syntax error in a sourced file fails the source and goes on
script:
. ./bad.sh
echo "after: $?"

name: A syntax error in a sourced file ends a POSIX shell
script:
set -o posix
. ./bad.sh
echo "after: $?"

name: File extended tests
script:
[[ -a /tmp ]] && echo "-a correctly checked /tmp"
[[ -a /some/non/existent/path ]] || echo "-a correctly checked non-existent path"

[[ -c /dev/null ]] && echo "-c correctly checked /dev/null"

name: Existence tests
script:
[[ -e '' ]] || echo "-e correctly identified empty string as non-existent"

[[ -e non-existent ]] || echo "-e correctly identified non-existent path"
[[ ! -e non-existent ]] && echo "! -e correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
[[ -e test-file ]] && echo "-e correctly identified existing non-dir"

mkdir test-dir
[[ -e test-dir ]] && echo "-d correctly identified existing dir"

name: Directory tests
script:
[[ -d '' ]] || echo "-d correctly identified empty string as non-existent"

[[ -d non-existent ]] || echo "-d correctly identified non-existent path"
[[ ! -d non-existent ]] && echo "! -d correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
[[ -d test-file ]] || echo "-d correctly identified non-dir file"

mkdir test-dir
[[ -d test-dir ]] && echo "-d correctly identified existing dir"

name: File regular tests
script:
[[ -f '' ]] || echo "-f correctly identified empty string as non-existent"

[[ -f non-existent ]] || echo "-f correctly identified non-existent path"
[[ ! -f non-existent ]] && echo "! -f correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
[[ -f test-file ]] && echo "-f correctly identified regular file"

mkdir test-dir
[[ -f test-dir ]] || echo "-f correctly identified directory as non-regular file"

name: File symbolic link tests
script:
[[ -L non-existent ]] || echo "-L correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
[[ -L test-file ]] || echo "-L correctly identified non-link file"

ln -s test-file valid-link
[[ -L valid-link ]] && echo "-L correctly identified valid symbolic link"

ln -s non-existent-target dangling-link
[[ -L dangling-link ]] && echo "-L correctly identified dangling symbolic link"

name: File sticky bit tests
script:
touch test-file
[[ -k test-file ]] || echo "-k correctly identified file without sticky bit"

chmod 1600 test-file
[[ -k test-file ]] && echo "-k correctly identified file with sticky bit"

name: Fifo test
script:
touch test-file
[[ -p test-file ]] || echo "-p correctly identified non-fifo file"

mkfifo fifo-file
[[ -p test-file ]] && echo "-p correctly identified fifo file"

name: File executable tests
script:
[[ -x non-existent ]] || echo "-x correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
ln -sf link test-file
[[ -x test-file ]] || echo "-x correctly identified non-executable file"
[[ -x link ]] || echo "-x correctly identified link to non-executable file"

chmod o+x test-file
[[ -x test-file ]] || echo "-x correctly identified other-only-executable file"
[[ -x link ]] || echo "-x correctly identified link to other-only-executable file"

chmod a+x test-file
[[ -x test-file ]] && echo "-x correctly identified executable file"
[[ -x link ]] && echo "-x correctly identified link to executable file"

name: File writable tests
script:
[[ -w non-existent ]] || echo "-w correctly identified non-existent path"

touch test-file
ln -sf link test-file
[[ -w test-file ]] || echo "-w correctly identified non-writable file"
[[ -w link ]] || echo "-w correctly identified link to non-writable file"

chmod o+x test-file
[[ -w test-file ]] || echo "-w correctly identified other-only-writable file"
[[ -w link ]] || echo "-w correctly identified link to other-only-writable file"

chmod a+x test-file
[[ -w test-file ]] && echo "-w correctly identified writable file"
[[ -w link ]] && echo "-w correctly identified link to writable file"

name: Variable set and nameref tests
script:
foo="bar"
declare -n bang=foo
[[ -R bang ]] && echo "-R correctly identified nameref variable that is set"

declare -n somevar
[[ -R somevar ]] || echo "-R correctly identified nameref variable that isn't set"

name: Files refer to same device and inode tests
script:
[[ /bin/sh -ef /bin/sh ]] && echo "-ef correctly identified device and inode numbers"

[[ ! /etc/os-release -ef /bin/sh ]] && echo "-ef correctly identified device and inode numbers that do not match"

name: File is newer
script:

[[ foo -nt bar ]] && echo "-nt correctly identified newer file"

[[ foo -nt file_no_exists ]] && echo "-nt correctly identified when file2 does not exist"

name: File is older
script:
touch -d "2 hours ago" foo
touch bar

[[ foo -ot bar ]] && echo "-ot correctly identified older file"
[[ foo -ot foo ]] && echo "-ot incorrectly identified file as older than itself"
[[ file_no_exists -ot foo ]] && echo "-ot correctly identified when file1 does not exist"

name: Unary string extended tests
script:
[[ -z "" ]] && echo "-z: Pass"
[[ -z "something" ]] && echo "-z: Fail"

[[ -n "something" ]] && echo "-n: Pass"
[[ -n "" ]] && echo "-n: Fail"

name: Shell option extended tests
script:

[[ -o emacs ]] && echo "1: option enabled"

[[ -o emacs ]] && echo "2: option enabled"

name: Binary string matching
script:
[[ "abc" == a* ]] && echo "1. Pass"
[[ "abc" != a* ]] && echo "2. Fail"
[[ a* != "abc" ]] && echo "3. Pass"

name: Binary string matching with expansion
script:
exclude="0123456789"
[[ "clue" == +([$exclude]) ]] && echo "1. Fail"
[[ "8675309" == +([$exclude]) ]] && echo "2. Pass"

name: Quoted pattern binary string matching
script:
[[ "abc" == "a*" ]] && echo "1. Matches"
[[ "abc" != "a*" ]] && echo "2. Matches"

name: Arithmetic extended tests
script:
[[ 0 -eq 0 ]] && echo "1. Pass"
[[ 0 -ne 0 ]] && echo "2. Fail"
[[ 0 -lt 0 ]] && echo "3. Fail"
[[ 0 -le 0 ]] && echo "4. Pass"
[[ 0 -gt 0 ]] && echo "5. Fail"
[[ 0 -ge 0 ]] && echo "6. Pass"

[[ 0 -eq 1 ]] && echo "7. Fail"
[[ 0 -ne 1 ]] && echo "8. Pass"
[[ 0 -lt 1 ]] && echo "9. Pass"
[[ 0 -le 1 ]] && echo "10. Pass"
[[ 0 -gt 1 ]] && echo "11. Fail"
[[ 0 -ge 1 ]] && echo "12. Fail"

[[ 1 -eq 0 ]] && echo "13. Fail"
[[ 1 -ne 0 ]] && echo "14. Pass"
[[ 1 -lt 0 ]] && echo "15. Fail"
[[ 1 -le 0 ]] && echo "16. Fail"
[[ 1 -gt 0 ]] && echo "17. Pass"
[[ 1 -ge 0 ]] && echo "18. Pass"

name: Regex
script:
[[ "a" =~ ^a$ ]]   && echo "1. Pass"
[[ "abc" =~ a* ]]  && echo "2. Pass"
[[ a =~ ^(a)$ ]]   && echo "3. Pass"
[[ a =~ ^(a|b)$ ]] && echo "4. Pass"
[[ a =~ c ]]       && echo "5. Pass"

name: Regex with leading ] in bracket expression
script:
[[ "]" =~ ^[]]$   ]] && echo "1. Matched"
[[ "a" =~ ^[]a]$  ]] && echo "2. Matched"
[[ "[" =~ ^[][]$  ]] && echo "3. Matched"
[[ "]" =~ ^[][]$  ]] && echo "4. Matched"
[[ "a" =~ ^[][]$  ]] || echo "5. Not matched"
[[ "[" =~ ^[^][]$ ]] || echo "6. Not matched"
[[ "a" =~ ^[^][]$ ]] && echo "7. Matched"
[[ "[" =~ ^[]a[]$ ]] && echo "8. Matched"
# Only the first '^' negates; the second is an ordinary member, so the ']'
# that follows it does terminate the expression.
[[ "xa" =~ ^[^^][ab]$ ]] && echo "9. Matched"
[[ "x[" =~ ^[^^][ab]$ ]] || echo "10. Not matched"
[[ "x]" =~ ^[^^]]$    ]] && echo "11. Matched"
# That leading ']' can also be the low end of a range.
[[ "^" =~ ^[]-a]$ ]] && echo "12. Matched"
[[ "]" =~ ^[]-a]$ ]] && echo "13. Matched"
[[ "-" =~ ^[]-a]$ ]] || echo "14. Not matched"
[[ "b" =~ ^[]-a]$ ]] || echo "15. Not matched"
echo "done"

name: Regex with '-' as a range endpoint
script:
for s in '+' ',' '-' '.' '/' 'a'; do
  [[ "$s" =~ ^[+--]$ ]] && echo "1. matched: $s"
done
for s in '+' ',' '-' '.' '/' 'a'; do
  [[ "$s" =~ ^[--/]$ ]] && echo "2. matched: $s"
done
echo "done"

name: Regex with case insensitivity
script:
shopt -u nocasematch
[[ "a" =~ A ]] && echo "1. Pass"

name: Regex with capture
script:
pattern='(Hello), ([a-z]+)\.'
if [[ "Hello, world." =~ ${pattern} ]]; then
    echo "Match found!"
    for i in "${!BASH_REMATCH[@]}"; do
        echo "$i: '${BASH_REMATCH[$i]}'"
    done
fi

name: Regex with capture including optional matches
script:
pattern='(Hello)(,?) ([a-z]+)\.'
if [[ "Hello world." =~ ${pattern} ]]; then
    echo "Match found!"
    for i in "${!BASH_REMATCH[@]}"; do
        echo "$i: '${BASH_REMATCH[$i]}'"
    done
fi

regex="^$"

[[ "" =~ ^$         ]] && echo "5. Matched"

Empty and space checks

set -- {a,b}{c,d}
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done

name: Brace expansion under IFS=: still splits the expansions inside it
script:
IFS=:
v="1:2"
set -- {$v,x}
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done

name: Brace expansion under IFS=: with quoted array[*] inside the list
script:
IFS=:
arr=(1 2)
set -- {"${arr[*]}",z}
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done

name: Brace expansion under IFS=: with tilde prefix
script:
IFS=:
set -- ~/{x,y}
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done

name: Empty IFS joins "$*" with no separator
script:
set -- a b c
IFS=
echo "[$*]"
x="$*"
echo "[$x]"
arr=(1 2 3)
echo "[${arr[*]}]"
y=${arr[*]}
echo "[$y]"

name: Unset IFS joins "$*" with a space
script:
set -- a b c
unset IFS
echo "[$*]"
arr=(1 2 3)
echo "[${arr[*]}]"

name: Empty IFS join inside a larger double-quoted word
script:
set -- a b c
IFS=
echo "[<$*>]"
echo "[${#*}]"
case "$*" in abc) echo joined;; *) echo "not joined";; esac

name: Literal word text is not field-split
script:
IFS=:
set -- a:b
echo "Count: $#"
set -- {a:b,c}
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done
set -- a:$'b'
echo "Count: $#"

name: Literal word text still globs under a non-default IFS
script:
IFS=:
set -- a:*
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done
IFS='*'
set -- a:*
echo "Count: $#"

name: Expansion result adjacent to literal text
script:
IFS=:
x="1:2"
set -- $x:3
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done
x="1:"
set -- $x:3
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done
set -- pre:$x
echo "Count: $#"
for arg in "$@"; do echo "[$arg]"; done

name: Default and alternate value words are split like any expansion result
compgen -W splits its word list on IFS
script:
IFS=:
compgen -W 'a:b c'
v="p:q"
compgen -W "$v"

name: Basic interactive test
script:
#expect-prompt
echo hi
#send:Enter
#expect:hi
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: SIGINT ends the command an interactive shell is running
script:
#expect-prompt
kill -INT $$; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: Programs inherit an ignored SIGINT after the shell first waits for one
script:
#expect-prompt
exec sh -c 'p=$1; shift; trap "" INT; exec env PS1="$p" "$0" --norc --noprofile -i "$@"' "$BASH" "$PS1" ${BRUSH_VERSION:+--no-config --disable-bracketed-paste --disable-color --input-backend=basic}
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
sh -c 'exit 0'; sh -c 'kill -INT $$; touch survived.txt'; echo "done-$((2 + 2))"
#send:Enter
#expect:done-4
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: An interactive shell's inherited _ isn't exported by its first prompt
script:
#expect-prompt
exec env _=/inherited/underscore PS1="$PS1" "$BASH" --norc --noprofile -i ${BRUSH_VERSION:+--no-config --disable-bracketed-paste --disable-color --input-backend=basic}
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
exec printenv _ > out.txt
#send:Enter

name: Simple tab completion
script:
#expect-prompt
cat test-file.
#send:Tab
#send:Enter
#expect:Hello, world.
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: PROMPT_COMMAND
script:
declare -a calls=()
command=0

PROMPT_COMMAND='calls+=("$command")'

command=first
command=second
command=third

unset PROMPT_COMMAND

declare -p calls

name: PROMPT_COMMAND in a non-interactive shell reading stdin
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND='echo PROMPT-COMMAND-RAN'
echo one
echo two

name: prompt expansion in a non-interactive shell reading stdin
script:
PS1='$(echo PS1-EXPANDED >&2)$ '
echo one
echo two

name: PS0 expansion in a non-interactive shell reading stdin
script:
PS0='$(echo PS0-EXPANDED >&2)'
echo one
echo two

name: PROMPT_COMMAND preserves the last argument in $_
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND='true PC-ARG'
true USER-ARG
echo "UNDERSCORE[$_]"
unset PROMPT_COMMAND

name: PROMPT_COMMAND as an indexed array
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND=('echo INDEXED-0' 'echo INDEXED-1')
echo command-ran
unset PROMPT_COMMAND

name: PROMPT_COMMAND array elements each see the last command's status
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND=('false' 'echo PC-SAW[$?]')
(exit 6)
echo "AFTER[$?]"
unset PROMPT_COMMAND

name: exit from PROMPT_COMMAND ends the shell with its status
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND=('echo PC-A' 'exit 7' 'echo PC-C')
echo NEVER-RUNS

name: PROMPT_COMMAND as an associative array is ignored
script:
declare -A PROMPT_COMMAND
PROMPT_COMMAND[x]='echo ASSOC-X'
PROMPT_COMMAND[y]='echo ASSOC-Y'
echo command-ran
unset PROMPT_COMMAND

name: return does not exit the shell, from PROMPT_COMMAND or the prompt
script:
PROMPT_COMMAND=('echo PC-A' 'return' 'echo PC-B')
echo STILL-ALIVE
unset PROMPT_COMMAND
return
echo STILL-ALIVE-AFTER-BARE-RETURN

name: prompt expansion preserves the last argument in $_
script:
PS1='$(true PS1-ARG)$ '
true USER-ARG
echo "UNDERSCORE[$_]"

name: prompt expansion preserves $? and PIPESTATUS
script:
PS1='$( (exit 9) | (exit 8) )$ '
(exit 4) | (exit 5)
echo "AFTER[$?][${PIPESTATUS[*]}]"

name: Interactive -c running a program
script: #expect:done

script:

f() { set -u; echo "$unset_var"; }; f; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal error in a builtin drops the rest of the interactive line

set -u; compgen -W '$unset_var'; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal error in a builtin ends an interactive shell's subshell
script:

( set -u; compgen -W '$unset_var'; touch went-on.txt )
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal expansion error drops the rest of the interactive line
script:
#expect-prompt
set -u; echo "$unset_var"; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal expansion error ends an interactive shell's subshell
script:
#expect-prompt
( set -u; echo "$unset_var"; touch went-on.txt )
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal error in eval drops only the eval'd code in an interactive shell
script:
#expect-prompt
set -u; eval 'echo "$unset_var"; touch skipped.txt'; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: A fatal error in a sourced file drops only that file in an interactive shell
script:
#expect-prompt
set -u; . ./script.sh; touch went-on.txt
#send:Enter
#expect-prompt
#send:Ctrl+D

name: Line continuation inside operators
script:
true &\
& echo and
false |\
| echo or
echo pipe |\
& cat
case x in x) echo case ;\
; esac
cat <\
<EOF
body
EOF

name: Line number after a line continuation
script:
true && \
  echo $LINENO
true | \
  echo $LINENO

name: Line number of a word after a line continuation
script:
echo \
  $LINENO

name: Line continuation after a dollar sign
script:
x=1
echo $\
(echo cmdsub) $\
{x} $\
x $\
((1 + 1)) $\
'ansi'

name: Line continuation in quotes
script:
echo "a\
b" 'c\
d' "e\\
f"
printf '[%s]\n' $'g\
h'

name: Line continuation in an extglob
script:
shopt -s extglob
case ab in @(a\
b)) echo unquoted;; esac
case ab in @("a\
b")) echo double-quoted;; esac
case 'a\
b' in @('a\
b')) echo single-quoted;; esac

name: Line continuation in single quotes in a parameter expansion in double quotes
script:
echo "${x:-'a\
b'}"

name: Ignore single quote in comment in list
script:
(
  # I'm
  echo "Batman"
)

name: Ignore double quote in comment in list
script:
(
  # This " is not being
  echo "parsed"
)

name: Ignore parentheses in comment in list

(
  # :(
  echo "Sad"
)

name: Ignore dollar in comment in list
script:
(
  #               $
  echo "Mr. Crabs ^"
)

name: Nameref basic read
script:
target="hello world"
declare -n ref=target
echo "ref: $ref"
echo "target: $target"

name: Nameref write through reference
script:
target="original"
declare -n ref=target
echo "before: $target"
ref="modified"
echo "after: $target"
echo "ref: $ref"

name: Nameref append with +=
script:
target="hello"
declare -n ref=target
ref+=" world"
echo "target: $target"
echo "ref: $ref"

name: Nameref to unset variable
script:
declare -n ref=nonexistent
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
echo "ref set: '${ref+SET}'"
ref="now exists"
echo "ref: $ref"
echo "nonexistent: $nonexistent"

name: Nameref reassignment - change target
script:
var1="first"
var2="second"
declare -n ref=var1
echo "ref -> var1: $ref"
ref=var2
echo "var1 after: $var1"
# To change what a nameref points to, use declare -n again
declare -n ref=var2
echo "ref -> var2: $ref"

name: Nameref chained (A -> B -> C)
script:
ultimate="final_value"
declare -n middle=ultimate
declare -n top=middle
echo "top: $top"
echo "middle: $middle"
top="changed"
echo "ultimate: $ultimate"

name: Nameref circular reference
script:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
echo "a: '${a}'"
echo "done"

name: Nameref self-reference
script:
declare -n self=self
echo "self: '${self}'"
echo "done"

name: Nameref in function - pass by reference
script:
modify_var() {
    local -n ref=$1
    ref="modified by function"
}

myvar="original"
echo "before: $myvar"
modify_var myvar
echo "after: $myvar"

name: Nameref in function scope - local nameref to outer var
script:
outer="outer_value"
inner_func() {
    local -n ref=outer
    echo "inside func: $ref"
    ref="modified_by_func"
}
echo "before: $outer"
inner_func
echo "after: $outer"

name: Nameref in function - multiple namerefs (swap)
script:
swap() {
    local -n x=$1
    local -n y=$2
    local tmp="$x"
    x="$y"
    y="$tmp"
}
a="alpha"
b="beta"
echo "before: a=$a b=$b"
swap a b
echo "after: a=$a b=$b"

name: Nameref with export
script:
target="exported_val"
declare -n ref=target
export ref
declare -p target | grep -o 'x' | head -1 || echo "no export flag"

name: Nameref unset through ref removes target
script:
target="value"
declare -n ref=target
echo "before: target=$target ref=$ref"
unset ref
echo "after: target='${target}' ref='${ref}'"
# ref still exists as a nameref, but target is gone
declare -p ref 2>/dev/null && echo "ref still declared"
declare -p target 2>/dev/null || echo "target is gone"

name: Nameref unset target directly
script:
target="exists"
declare -n ref=target
echo "ref: $ref"
unset target
echo "ref after unset: '${ref}'"

name: Nameref array append with +=
script:
target=(a b)
declare -n ref=target
ref+=(c d)
echo "target: ${target[@]}"
echo "count: ${#target[@]}"
declare -p target

name: Nameref array element unset
script:
target=(a b c d)
declare -n ref=target
unset 'ref[2]'
declare -p target

name: Nameref array slicing
script:
target=(a b c d e)
declare -n ref=target
echo "slice: ${ref[@]:1:2}"
echo "all: ${ref[@]}"
echo "count: ${#ref[@]}"

name: Nameref to array element
script:
arr=(zero one two three)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
echo "ref: $ref"
ref="changed"
echo "arr[2]: ${arr[2]}"

name: Nameref in subshell
script:
target="original"
declare -n ref=target
(ref="subshell_value"; echo "inside: $target")
echo "outside: $target"

name: Nameref in command substitution
script:
target="original"
declare -n ref=target
result=$(ref="cmd_sub_value"; echo "$target")
echo "result: $result"
echo "target: $target"

name: Nameref with integer attribute
script:
target=0
declare -ni ref=target
ref="hello"
echo "target: $target"
ref=42
echo "target: $target"
declare -p ref
declare -p target

name: Nameref with set -u and unset target
script:
set -u
declare -n ref=unset_target
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

name: Nameref to empty string target name
script:
declare -n ref=""
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
ref="value" 2>/dev/null
echo "done"

name: Multiple namerefs to same target
script:
target="initial"
declare -n ref1=target
declare -n ref2=target
ref1="from_ref1"
echo "ref2: $ref2"
echo "target: $target"
ref2="from_ref2"
echo "ref1: $ref1"
echo "target: $target"

name: Circular reference in assignment context
script:
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
a="value" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

name: Nameref with prefix enumeration
script:
declare -n ref_one=target1
declare -n ref_two=target2
regular_ref_var="not a nameref"
echo "prefix: ${!ref_@}"

name: Nameref with local in nested functions
Nameref for-in loop changes target
script:
var1="a"
var2="b"
var3="c"
declare -n ref
for ref in var1 var2 var3; do
    echo "ref=$ref"
done
echo "var1=$var1 var2=$var2 var3=$var3"

name: Nameref to array element - arithmetic increment
script:
arr=(10 20 30 40)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
echo "before: $ref"
(( ref++ ))
echo "after: $ref"
echo "arr[2]: ${arr[2]}"

name: Nameref to array element - arithmetic compound assign
script:
arr=(100 200 300)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "before: $ref"
(( ref += 50 ))
echo "after: $ref"
echo "arr[1]: ${arr[1]}"

name: Nameref to array element - arithmetic expression
script:
arr=(100 200 300)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
(( ref = ref * 2 ))
echo "arr[2]: ${arr[2]}"

name: Nameref to array element - string append
script:
arr=(hello world)
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
ref+=" there"
echo "arr[0]: ${arr[0]}"

name: Nameref to array element - length
script:
arr=("short" "a longer string here" "x")
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "len: ${#ref}"

name: Nameref to array element - parameter transformations
script:
arr=("hello world" "foo")
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
echo "upper: ${ref^^}"
echo "Q: ${ref@Q}"

name: Nameref to array element - substring
script:
arr=("abcdefgh" "xyz")
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
echo "sub: ${ref:1:3}"

name: Nameref to array element - pattern substitution
script:
arr=("hello world hello" "x")
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
echo "first: ${ref/hello/bye}"
echo "all: ${ref//hello/bye}"

name: Nameref to array element - default value
script:
arr=("" "val")
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
echo "default: ${ref:-fallback}"

name: Nameref to array element - negative index
script:
arr=(a b c d e)
declare -n ref='arr[-1]'
echo "ref: $ref"

name: Nameref to associative array element
script:
declare -A map=([foo]=bar [baz]=qux)
declare -n ref='map[foo]'
echo "ref: $ref"
ref="changed"
echo "map_foo: ${map[foo]}"

name: Nameref to array element - unset through ref
script:
arr=(a b c d)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
unset ref
declare -p arr

name: Nameref chain 4 levels
script:
final="deep"
declare -n c=final
declare -n b=c
declare -n a=b
echo "a: $a"
a="changed"
echo "final: $final"

name: Nameref 3-level chain to array element
script:
arr=(A B C)
declare -n mid='arr[1]'
declare -n top=mid
echo "top: $top"
top="CHANGED"
echo "arr[1]: ${arr[1]}"

name: Nameref to associative array - keys and values
script:
declare -A map=([x]=1 [y]=2)
declare -n ref=map
echo "x: ${ref[x]}"
ref[z]=3
echo "z: ${map[z]}"
for k in "${!ref[@]}"; do echo "key=$k"; done | sort

name: Nameref - declare -p shows nameref attribute
script:
target="hello"
declare -n ref=target
declare -p ref
declare -p target

name: Nameref - test -v follows nameref
script:
declare -n ref=nonesuch
[[ -v ref ]] && echo "set" || echo "unset"
nonesuch="now"
[[ -v ref ]] && echo "set" || echo "unset"

name: Nameref to array - length and keys
script:
arr=(a b c d e)
declare -n ref=arr
echo "len: ${#ref[@]}"
echo "keys: ${!ref[@]}"
echo "elem0len: ${#ref}"

name: Nameref with printf -v
script:
declare -n ref=formatted
printf -v ref "num=%d" 42
echo "formatted: $formatted"

name: Nameref - declare +n removes attribute
script:
target="value"
declare -n ref=target
echo "before: $ref"
declare +n ref
echo "after: $ref"
declare -p ref

name: Nameref to IFS
script:
declare -n ref=IFS
saved="$IFS"
ref=":"
echo "ifs: '$IFS'"
IFS="$saved"

name: Nameref to array - whole array assignment
script:
declare -n ref=myarr
ref=(x y z)
declare -p myarr

name: Nameref local -n recursive function
script:
count_down() {
    local v=$1
    if (( v <= 0 )); then return; fi
    local -n o=result
    o+="$v "
    count_down $((v - 1))
}
result=""
count_down 3
echo "result: $result"

name: Nameref to array - negative index access
script:
arr=(a b c d e)
declare -n ref=arr
echo "last: ${ref[-1]}"

name: Nameref in eval
script:
target="eval_val"
declare -n ref=target
eval 'echo "eval: $ref"'

name: Nameref in here-string
script:
target="here_data"
declare -n ref=target
cat <<< "$ref"

name: Nameref in extended test operators
script:
target="abc"
declare -n ref=target
[[ $ref == abc ]] && echo "eq ok"
[[ $ref =~ ^a.c$ ]] && echo "regex ok"
[[ $ref < bcd ]] && echo "lt ok"

name: Nameref to sparse array
script:
declare -a arr
arr[5]=five
arr[10]=ten
declare -n ref=arr
echo "keys: ${!ref[@]}"
echo "len: ${#ref[@]}"
echo "elem5: ${ref[5]}"

name: Nameref concurrent writes through two refs
script:
target="init"
declare -n r1=target
declare -n r2=target
r1+="_one"
r2+="_two"
echo "target: $target"

name: Nameref to array element - ternary in arithmetic
script:
arr=(0 1 0)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "ternary: $(( ref ? 100 : 200 ))"

name: Nameref chain to assoc array element
script:
declare -A map=([k]=v)
declare -n mid='map[k]'
declare -n top=mid
echo "top: $top"

name: Nameref to array element - set test
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "set: ${ref+SET}"
unset 'arr[1]'
echo "unset: ${ref+SET}"

name: Nameref local -n overrides outer nameref
script:
a="A"
b="B"
declare -n ref=a
f() {
    local -n ref=b
    echo "inner: $ref"
}
f
echo "outer: $ref"

name: Nameref target lowercase transform
script:
declare -l target=""
declare -n ref=target
ref="HELLO"
echo "target: $target"

name: Nameref export -n unexports target
script:
export target="val"
declare -n ref=target
export -n ref
env | grep "^target=" | head -1 || echo "not exported"

name: Nameref to array - push via index
script:
arr=(a b)
declare -n ref=arr
ref[${#ref[@]}]="c"
echo "arr: ${ref[@]}"
echo "len: ${#ref[@]}"

name: Nameref with readonly target - write fails
script:
target="immutable"
declare -n ref=target
readonly ref
ref="attempt" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
echo "target: $target"

name: Nameref - declare -a through nameref applies to target
script:
declare -n ref=myarr
declare -a ref
ref=(1 2 3)
declare -p myarr 2>/dev/null || echo "not found"

name: Nameref - declare -A through nameref applies to target
script:
declare -n ref=mymap
declare -A ref
ref=([a]=1 [b]=2)
echo "a: ${mymap[a]}"
echo "b: ${mymap[b]}"

name: Nameref to array element - test -v treats resolved name literally
script:
# In bash, [[ -v ref ]] where ref→arr[2] looks for a variable literally
# named "arr[2]", not array element arr at index 2. So it's always unset.
arr=(a b c d)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
echo "ref expands to: $ref"
[[ -v ref ]] && echo "set" || echo "unset"
unset 'arr[2]'
[[ -v ref ]] && echo "set" || echo "unset"

name: Nameref to array element - test -v with nonexistent index
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[5]'
[[ -v ref ]] && echo "set" || echo "unset"

name: Nameref to arr[@] expands all elements
script:
arr=(x y z)
declare -n ref='arr[@]'
echo "ref: $ref"

name: Nameref circular with 3 nodes
script:
declare -n c1=c2
declare -n c2=c3
declare -n c3=c1
echo "c1: '${c1}'"
echo "exit: $?"

name: Nameref in case pattern
Nameref local shadowing in nested functions
script:
a="A"
b="B"
f() {
    local -n ref=a
    g
    echo "f ref: $ref"
}
g() {
    local -n ref=b
    echo "g ref: $ref"
    ref="modified_B"
}
f
echo "a=$a b=$b"

name: Nameref to special variable RANDOM
script:
declare -n ref=RANDOM
r1=$ref
r2=$ref
[[ "$r1" != "$r2" ]] && echo "different (dynamic)" || echo "same"

name: Nameref for-in loop retargets through iteration
script:
var1="A"
var2="B"
var3="C"
declare -n ref
for ref in var1 var2 var3; do
    echo "ref=$ref"
done
echo "var1=$var1 var2=$var2 var3=$var3"

name: Nameref declared without value - bare declare -n
script:
declare -n ref
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
declare -p ref 2>/dev/null
ref="value"
echo "ref after assign: '${ref}'"
declare -p ref 2>/dev/null

name: Nameref declared without value - expansion behavior
script:
declare -n ref
echo "set: ${ref+SET}"
echo "default: ${ref:-fallback}"
echo "length: ${#ref}"

name: Nameref to numeric-only target name
script:
declare -n ref=123
echo "exit: $?"
echo "ref: '${ref}'"
echo "done"

name: Nameref to name with special characters
script:
declare -n ref="a-b"
echo "exit1: $?"
declare -n ref2="a.b"
echo "exit2: $?"
declare -n ref3="a+b"
echo "exit3: $?"
echo "done"

name: Nameref to name with spaces
script:
declare -n ref="a b"
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

name: Nameref to positional parameter name
script:
declare -n ref=1
