name: Arithmetic (( )) with subscripted nameref
script:
arr=(100 200 300)
declare -n ref='arr[0]'
(( ref += 50 ))
echo "arr[0]: ${arr[0]}"
echo "expr: $(( ref * 2 ))"

name: String length through subscripted nameref
script:
arr=("short" "a longer string here" "x")
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "len: ${#ref}"

name: Long nameref chain (8 levels - at bash max)
script:
final_target="deep_value"
declare -n c8=final_target
declare -n c7=c8
declare -n c6=c7
declare -n c5=c6
declare -n c4=c5
declare -n c3=c4
declare -n c2=c3
declare -n c1=c2
echo "c1: $c1"
c1="changed"
echo "final_target: $final_target"

name: Nameref chain exceeds max depth
script:
final_target="deep_value"
declare -n c9=final_target
declare -n c8=c9
declare -n c7=c8
declare -n c6=c7
declare -n c5=c6
declare -n c4=c5
declare -n c3=c4
declare -n c2=c3
declare -n c1=c2
echo "c1: '$c1'"
echo "done"

name: Declare -x through subscripted nameref applies to base
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[2]'
declare -x ref 2>/dev/null
declare -p arr 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'x' || echo "no export"

name: Exported nameref passes literal value to child
script:
target="value"
declare -nx myref=target
# The nameref's literal value (the target name) is exported to child
bash -c 'echo "myref: $myref"'
# The target itself needs separate export
export target
bash -c 'echo "target: $target"'

name: Subscripted nameref with set -u when element is set
script:
set -u
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
echo "ref: $ref"

name: Subscripted nameref with set -u when element is unset
script:
set -u
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[5]'
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

name: Nameref with := default creates target through nameref
script:
declare -n ref=new_var
echo "before: '${new_var:-}'"
result="${ref:=hello}"
echo "result: $result"
echo "new_var: $new_var"

name: Nameref with := default when target exists but is empty
script:
target=""
declare -n ref=target
result="${ref:=fallback}"
echo "result: $result"
echo "target: $target"

name: Readonly nameref in for-in loop fails
script:
declare -n ref=var1
readonly ref
for ref in a b c; do
    echo "should not print: $ref"
done
echo "exit: $?"
echo "done"

name: Circular nameref with set -e does not abort script
script:
set -e
declare -n a=b
declare -n b=a
echo "val: '${a}'"
echo "script continues"

name: Nameref to unset variable with set -eu errors and exits
script:
set -eu
declare -n ref=nonexistent
echo "$ref"
echo "should not print"

name: Export through subscripted nameref is rejected by bash
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
export ref 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"
declare -p arr | grep -o 'x' | head -1 || echo "no export"

name: Readonly through subscripted nameref makes base readonly
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
readonly ref
declare -p arr
arr[0]="new" 2>/dev/null
echo "exit: $?"

name: Declare -p on subscripted nameref shows nameref itself
script:
arr=(a b c)
declare -n ref='arr[1]'
declare -p ref
echo "ref value: $ref"

name: basic redirection to fd 3
script:
exec 3>trace.txt
BASH_XTRACEFD=3

set -x
echo "hello"
echo "world"

set +x
cat trace.txt

name: redirection takes effect immediately
script:
exec 3>trace.txt

set -x
echo "before setting BASH_XTRACEFD"

BASH_XTRACEFD=3
echo "after setting BASH_XTRACEFD"

set +x

echo "Content of trace file:"
cat trace.txt

name: unsetting BASH_XTRACEFD returns to stderr
script:
exec 3>trace.txt
BASH_XTRACEFD=3

set -x
echo "redirected"

unset BASH_XTRACEFD
echo "back to stderr"

set +x

echo "Content of trace file:"
cat trace.txt

name: invalid fd value falls back to stderr
script:
BASH_XTRACEFD=999

set -x
echo "should go to stderr"

set +x

name: non-numeric value falls back to stderr
script:
BASH_XTRACEFD=invalid

set -x
echo "should go to stderr"

set +x

name: empty value falls back to stderr
script:
BASH_XTRACEFD=

set -x
echo "should go to stderr"

name: redirect to file that fails writes
script:
# This test relies on /dev/full being present. We degrade gracefully
# if it doesn't.
[[ -e /dev/full ]] || exit

exec 3>/dev/full
BASH_XTRACEFD=3

set -x
echo "first echo"
echo "first echo result: $?"

name: Default options
script: echo "Default options: $-"

name: errtrace disabled by default
script:
set +E 2>/dev/null || true
echo "errtrace test"

name: errtrace can be enabled and disabled
script:
set -E
echo "enabled: $-" | grep -q E && echo "E is set"
set +E
echo "disabled: $-" | grep -qv E && echo "E is unset"

name: errtrace disabled - functions don't inherit ERR trap
script:
set +E
trap 'echo "ERR trapped"' ERR
myfunc() { false; }
myfunc
echo "after"

name: errtrace enabled - functions inherit ERR trap
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR trapped"' ERR
myfunc() { false; }
myfunc
echo "after"

name: errtrace with nested functions
errtrace toggling mid-script
script:
trap 'echo "ERR trapped"' ERR
set -E
myfunc1() { false; }
myfunc1
echo "after first call"
set +E
myfunc2() { false; }
myfunc2
echo "after second call"

name: errtrace disabled - subshell doesn't inherit ERR trap
script:
set +E
trap 'echo "ERR"' ERR
(
  trap -p ERR
  false
  echo "no ERR trap fired"
)
echo "after"

name: errtrace enabled - subshell inherits ERR trap
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR"' ERR
(
  trap -p ERR | grep -q ERR && echo "ERR trap inherited"
  false
  echo "after false in subshell"
)
echo "after"

name: errtrace disabled - command substitution doesn't inherit ERR trap
script:
set +E
trap 'echo "[ERR trapped]" >&2' ERR
result=$(trap -p ERR; false; echo "no trap inherited")
echo "result: $result"

name: errtrace enabled - command substitution inherits ERR trap
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "[ERR in subshell]" >&2' ERR
result=$(false; echo "after false in subshell")
echo "result: $result"

name: errtrace with pipeline - last command fails
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "[ERR: $?]" >&2' ERR
echo "data" | cat | false
echo "after pipeline"

name: errtrace with pipeline - middle command fails (pipefail)
script:
set -E
set -o pipefail
trap 'echo "[ERR: $?]" >&2' ERR
echo "data" | false | cat
echo "after pipeline"

name: errtrace - ERR trap in pipeline subshells
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "[ERR: $BASH_COMMAND]" >&2' ERR
echo "input" | { false; echo "after false in brace"; }
echo "done"

name: errtrace with errexit - ERR trap fires before exit
script:
set -e
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR trap fired"' ERR
false
echo "should not print"

name: errtrace with errexit in function
script:
set -e
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR trap"' ERR
myfunc() { false; }
myfunc
echo "should not print"

name: errtrace - ERR trap in deeply nested function
errtrace - ERR trap can be changed inside function
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "outer ERR"' ERR
myfunc() {
  trap 'echo "inner ERR"' ERR
  false
}
myfunc
false
echo "after"

name: errtrace - ERR trap can be cleared inside function
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR"' ERR
myfunc() {
  trap - ERR
  false
  echo "no ERR in func"
}
myfunc
false
echo "after"

name: errtrace - ERR trap in background job
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR" >&2' ERR
{ false; echo "bg done"; } &
wait
echo "main done"

name: errtrace - ERR trap inherited in sourced script
script:
set -E
trap 'echo "ERR trapped"' ERR
. ./failing.sh
echo "after source"

name: extdebug implies functrace - DEBUG inherited in functions
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "in func"
}
echo "before"
myfunc
echo "after"

name: extdebug implies functrace - DEBUG inherited in subshells
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
echo "before"
(echo "in subshell")
echo "after"

name: DEBUG trap - returns 0 command executes normally
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'return 0' DEBUG
echo "line 1"
echo "line 2"
echo "line 3"

name: DEBUG trap - returns 1 command is skipped
script:
shopt -s extdebug
skip_next=false
trap '
  if $skip_next; then
    skip_next=false
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
' DEBUG
echo "line 1"
skip_next=true
echo "this should be skipped"
echo "line 3"

name: DEBUG trap - returns 2 simulates return from function
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap '
  if [[ "${FUNCNAME[0]}" == "myfunc" && "$BASH_COMMAND" == *"should not"* ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  return 0
' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "start of func"
  echo "this should not print"
  echo "also should not print"
}
myfunc
echo "after func: $?"

name: DEBUG trap - return value ignored without extdebug
script:
shopt -u extdebug
trap 'return 1' DEBUG
echo "line 1"
echo "line 2"
echo "line 3"

name: Skip simple command
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap '[[ "$BASH_COMMAND" == *"skip"* ]] && return 1; return 0' DEBUG
echo "keep this"
echo "skip this"
echo "keep this too"

name: Skip in loop - iteration skipped but loop continues
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap '[[ "$BASH_COMMAND" == *"skip"* ]] && return 1; return 0' DEBUG
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "iter $i"
  echo "skip $i"
  echo "after skip $i"
done
echo "done"

name: Skip in conditional
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap '[[ "$BASH_COMMAND" == *"skip"* ]] && return 1; return 0' DEBUG
if true; then
  echo "in then"
  echo "skip in then"
  echo "after skip in then"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Return 2 in nested function - unwinds to caller
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap '
  if [[ "${FUNCNAME[0]}" == "inner" && "$BASH_COMMAND" == *"inner cmd"* ]]; then
    return 2
  fi
  return 0
' DEBUG
inner() {
  echo "inner start"
  echo "inner cmd"
  echo "inner end"
}
outer() {
  echo "outer start"
  inner
  echo "outer after inner"
}
outer
echo "main after outer"

name: BASH_ARGC - contains argument counts per call frame
BASH_ARGV - contains arguments in reverse order
BASH_ARGC/ARGV - in nested calls
BASH_ARGC/ARGV - empty when no arguments
declare -F - shows function name only without extdebug
script:
myfunc() { echo hi; }
declare -F myfunc

name: declare -F - shows filename and line number with extdebug
script:
shopt -s extdebug
. ./funcs.sh
declare -F myfunc | sed 's/[0-9]*/N/'

name: extdebug with errexit - skipped command doesn't trigger errexit
script:
shopt -s extdebug
set -e
trap '[[ "$BASH_COMMAND" == "false" ]] && return 1; return 0' DEBUG
echo "before"
false
echo "after - should print because false was skipped"

name: extdebug disabled after being enabled
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'return 1' DEBUG
echo "line 1 - should be skipped"
shopt -u extdebug
echo "line 2 - should print"
echo "line 3 - should print"

name: extdebug with set -T - both affect DEBUG inheritance
script:
shopt -s extdebug
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "in func"
}
myfunc
echo "done"

name: DEBUG trap with extdebug in function
script:
shopt -s extdebug
count=0
trap '
  ((count++))
  echo "debug $count: $BASH_COMMAND"
  return 0
' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  local x=1
  echo "x=$x"
}
myfunc

name: DEBUG trap with extdebug controls command execution
script:
shopt -s extdebug
should_skip=false
trap '
  if $should_skip; then
    should_skip=false
    echo "[skipping: $BASH_COMMAND]"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
' DEBUG
echo "first"
should_skip=true
echo "second - will be skipped"
echo "third"

name: extdebug with recursive function
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'echo "depth: ${#FUNCNAME[@]}"' DEBUG
recurse() {
  local n=$1
  if ((n > 0)); then
    recurse $((n - 1))
  fi
}
recurse 3

name: BASH_COMMAND shows compound command
script:
shopt -s extdebug
trap 'echo "cmd: $BASH_COMMAND"' DEBUG
if true; then echo "in if"; fi

name: DEBUG trap can modify variables
script:
shopt -s extdebug
counter=0
trap '((counter++)); return 0' DEBUG
echo "a"
echo "b"
echo "c"
echo "counter: $counter"

name: functrace can be enabled and disabled
script:
set -T
echo "enabled: $-" | grep -q T && echo "T is set"
set +T
echo "disabled: $-" | grep -qv T && echo "T is unset"

name: DEBUG trap - does not fire in function without set -T
script:
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "in func"
}
echo "before func"
myfunc
echo "after func"

name: DEBUG trap - fires in function with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "in func"
}
echo "before func"
myfunc
echo "after func"

name: DEBUG trap - does not fire in subshell without set -T
script:
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
echo "before subshell"
(echo "in subshell")
echo "after subshell"

name: DEBUG trap - fires in subshell with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
echo "before subshell"
(echo "in subshell")
echo "after subshell"

name: DEBUG trap - does not fire in command substitution without set -T
script:
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]" >&2' DEBUG
echo "before"
result=$(echo "in substitution")
echo "result: $result"

name: DEBUG trap - fires in command substitution with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]" >&2' DEBUG
echo "before"
result=$(echo "in substitution")
echo "result: $result"

name: DEBUG trap - does not fire in pipeline without set -T
script:
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]" >&2' DEBUG
echo "before"
echo "hello" | cat | cat
echo "after"

name: DEBUG trap - fires in pipeline with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]" >&2' DEBUG
echo "before"
echo "hello" | cat | cat
echo "after"

name: RETURN trap - does not fire in called function without set -T
RETURN trap - fires in called function with set -T
RETURN trap - fires for each nested function return with set -T
declare -t - enables trace for specific function
declare +t - disables trace for specific function
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  echo "in func"
}
declare +t myfunc
echo "calling func"
myfunc
echo "done"

name: declare -f - shows trace attribute
set -T enabled mid-script affects subsequent calls
script:
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
func1() { echo "in func1"; }
func2() { echo "in func2"; }
echo "calling func1 without -T"
func1
set -T
echo "calling func2 with -T"
func2
echo "done"

name: set +T disables inheritance mid-script
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug: $BASH_COMMAND]"' DEBUG
func1() { echo "in func1"; }
func2() { echo "in func2"; }
echo "calling func1 with -T"
func1
set +T
echo "calling func2 without -T"
func2
echo "done"

name: DEBUG trap - in background job with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug]" >&2' DEBUG
{
  echo "in background"
} &
wait
echo "done"

name: DEBUG trap - in process substitution with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[debug]" >&2' DEBUG
cat <(echo "from procsub")
echo "done"

name: BASH_COMMAND in function with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "cmd: $BASH_COMMAND"' DEBUG
myfunc() {
  local v=10
  echo "v=$v"
}
myfunc

name: Outer function traced, inner function not traced
Only inner function traced
RETURN trap - fires for function in sourced script with set -T
script:
set -T
trap 'echo "[return: ${FUNCNAME:-main}]"' RETURN
. ./sourced.sh
echo "after source"

name: DEBUG trap - count in deeply nested function calls with set -T
inherit_errexit disabled by default
script: shopt -q inherit_errexit && echo "enabled" || echo "disabled"

name: inherit_errexit disabled - command substitution ignores errexit
script:
set -e
shopt -u inherit_errexit
result=$(false; echo "still running")
echo "result: $result"
echo "after"

name: inherit_errexit enabled - command substitution inherits errexit
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
result=$(false; echo "should not print")
echo "should not print"

name: inherit_errexit with nested command substitution
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
result=$(echo "outer: $(false; echo inner)")
echo "should not print"

name: inherit_errexit disabled - nested substitution continues
script:
set -e
shopt -u inherit_errexit
result=$(echo "outer: $(false; echo inner)")
echo "result: $result"
echo "after"

name: inherit_errexit with backtick substitution
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
result=`false; echo "should not print"`
echo "should not print"

name: inherit_errexit with assignment
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
var=$(false)
echo "should not print"

name: inherit_errexit in function
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
myfunc() {
  local result=$(false; echo "should not print")
  echo "after local"
}
myfunc
echo "should not print"

name: inherit_errexit toggling
script:
set -e
shopt -s inherit_errexit
result1=$(false; echo "should not print in first")
echo "should not print 1"

name: inherit_errexit with multiple commands in substitution
script:
set -e
shopt -u inherit_errexit
result=$(echo "start"; false; echo "after false")
echo "result: $result"
echo "after"

name: set -B
set -C
script:
touch existing-file

set -C

echo hi > non-existing-file
echo "Result (non existing): $?"
echo "File contents: $(cat non-existing-file)"
echo

echo hi > /dev/null
echo "Result (device file): $?"
echo

echo hi > existing-file
echo "Result (existing file): $?"
echo "File contents: $(cat existing-file)"
echo

echo hi >| existing-file
echo "Result (clobber): $?"
echo "File contents: $(cat existing-file)"
echo

name: set -a
script:
v1=1 v2=2 v3=3 v4=4 v5=(a b c)
declare -p v1 v2 v3 v4

set -a
v1=reassigned
v2+=appended
declare -i v3
v4+=(appended)
v5[2]=updated
v6=new
v7[0]=new
v8=(new)
declare v9=new
declare -a v10=(new)

declare -p v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v8 v9 v10

name: errexit with set -o errexit
script:
set -o errexit
false
echo "should not print"

name: errexit status check
script:
set -e
set -o | grep errexit

name: Basic non-error case
script:
set -e
true
echo "Text after call"

name: Basic error case
script:
set -e
false
echo "Text after call"

name: Command line -e
script:
false
echo "should not print"

name: Multiple commands before error
script:
set -e
echo "first"
echo "second"
false
echo "should not print"

name: Error in middle of script
script:
set -e
echo "before"
false
echo "after"

name: Error in if condition
script:
set -e
if false; then
  echo "then branch"
else
  echo "else branch"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Error in elif condition
script:
set -e
if false; then
  echo "then branch"
elif false; then
  echo "elif branch"
else
  echo "else branch"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Error in if body
script:
set -e
if true; then
  false
  echo "should not print"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Error in elif body
script:
set -e
if false; then
  echo "then branch"
elif true; then
  false
  echo "should not print"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Error in else body
script:
set -e
if false; then
  echo "then"
else
  false
  echo "should not print"
fi
echo "after if"

name: Error in if condition with compound test
script:
set -e
if false && false; then
  echo "then"
else
  echo "else"
fi
echo "after"

name: Error in while condition
script:
set -e
count=0
while false; do
  echo "loop body"
done
echo "after while"

name: Error in while body
script:
set -e
count=0
while [ $count -lt 2 ]; do
  count=$((count + 1))
  false
  echo "should not print"
done
echo "after while"

name: Error in until condition
script:
set -e
count=0
until true; do
  echo "loop body"
done
echo "after until"

name: Error in until body
script:
set -e
until false; do
  false
  echo "loop body"
  break
done
echo "after until"

name: Error on right side of &&
script:
set -e
true && false
echo "after &&"

name: Error on left side of &&
script:
set -e
false && true
echo "after &&"

name: Error on left side of && as the last command of a for loop
script:
set -e
for x in a; do false && true; done
echo "after for"

name: Error on both sides of ||
script:
set -e
false || false
echo "after ||"

name: Error on left side of ||
script:
set -e
false || true
echo "after ||"

name: Error on right side of ||
script:
set -e
true || false
echo "after ||"

name: Error after && chain
script:
set -e
true && true
false
echo "should not print"

name: Complex boolean expression
script:
set -e
false || true && false || true
echo "after complex expression"

name: Negated command with failure
script:
set -e
! false
echo "after negation"

name: Negated command with success
script:
set -e
! true
echo "after negation"

name: Error after negated command
script:
set -e
! false
false
echo "should not print"

name: Error in first command of pipeline (without pipefail)
script:
set -e
false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in first command of pipeline (without pipefail, negated)
script:
set -e
! false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in first command of pipeline (with pipefail)
script:
set -e -o pipefail
false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in first command of pipeline (with pipefail, negated)
script:
set -e -o pipefail
! false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in middle of pipeline (without pipefail)
script:
set -e
true | false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in middle of pipeline (without pipefail, negated)
script:
set -e
! true | false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in middle of pipeline (with pipefail)
script:
set -e -o pipefail
true | false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in middle of pipeline (with pipefail, negated)
script:
set -e -o pipefail
! true | false | true
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in last command of pipeline (without pipefail)
script:
set -e
true | false
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in last command of pipeline (without pipefail, negated)
script:
set -e
! true | false
echo "after pipeline"

name: Error in last command of pipeline (with pipefail)
script:

name: empty PATH entry is reported as the working directory
script:
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n' > prog
chmod +x prog
PATH=":$PATH"

echo "[type]"
type prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -p]"
type -p prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -P]"
type -P prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -a]"
type -a prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[command -v]"
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

name: empty PATH entry is reported the same wherever it appears
script:
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n' > prog
chmod +x prog
original=$PATH

# Each of these keeps the rest of PATH reachable, so only the empty entry can
# account for finding `prog`, which exists solely in the working directory.
echo "[leading]"
PATH=":$original"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

echo "[trailing]"
PATH="$original:"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

echo "[middle]"
PATH="/nonexistent::$original"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

name: empty PATH entry is hashed as the working directory
script:
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n' > prog
chmod +x prog
PATH=":$PATH"

hash -r
hash prog; echo "rc=$?"
hash -t prog; echo "rc=$?"

name: empty PATH entry is passed to the command as the working directory
script:
# A copy of env, found through the empty entry before the real one, reports the _
# it's started with: the path the shell ran it by. (It keeps env's name, which a
# multi-call binary such as NixOS's coreutils goes by.)
cp "$(command -v env)" env
PATH=":$PATH"

env | grep '^_='

name: command found through an empty PATH entry is searched for again after cd
script:
for first in "" "."; do
  export PATH="${first}:${PWD}/fallback:${PATH}"
  cd a
  prog
  hash -t prog; type prog
  cd ../b
  prog; echo "status: $?"
  cd ../a
  prog
  hash -t prog; type prog
  cd ..
  export PATH="${PATH#"${first}:${PWD}/fallback:"}"
done

done

test_pattern() {
  local str="$1"
  local pattern="$2"

  if [[ "${str}" == ${pattern} ]]; then
    echo "Matched: ${str} using ${pattern}"
  else
    echo "No match: ${str} using ${pattern}"
  fi
}

test_pattern "abc" "a*"

name: Realistic installer-shaped script
script:
set -e

INSTALL_DIR="./installed"

log() {
  echo "[install] $1"
}

detect_platform() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux*)
      echo linux
      ;;
    Darwin*)
      echo darwin
      ;;
    *)
      echo unknown
      ;;
  esac
}

main() {
  platform="$(detect_platform)"
  if [ -z "$platform" ]; then
    log "could not detect platform"
    exit 1
  fi

  mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR" &&
    log "created dir"

  cat >"$INSTALL_DIR/config" <<EOF
platform=detected
dir=$INSTALL_DIR
EOF

  while read -r line; do
    log "config: $line"
  done <"$INSTALL_DIR/config"

  log "done"
}

main

name: Backslash-CR survives prompt expansion (issue #1119)
script:
# OSC 133;C followed by ST (\e\\) and CR. The ST must end with a literal
# backslash byte (0x5c); without it, the OSC is malformed and terminals
# may eat the first character of subsequent output.
prompt='\e]133;C\e\\\r'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Backslash before non-special char preserves backslash
script:
# Under double-quote escape rules, a backslash before a non-special
# character is preserved literally. \\X (raw) = '\' + 'X' should expand
# to literal '\X'.
prompt='\\X'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt='\\Z'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt='\\n'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt=$'\\\\\t'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Backslash before dollar escapes parameter expansion
script:
# `\\$VAR` (PS0 raw chars: \\, $, V, A, R) → step 1 produces \$VAR, then
# step 2's `\$` consumes the backslash and leaves a literal $, so $VAR
# remains literal (not expanded).
var=hello
prompt='\\$var'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Double backslash before dollar yields backslash + expansion
script:
# `\\\\$VAR` → step 1 produces \\$VAR, then step 2's `\\` reduces to a
# literal `\` and `$VAR` is expanded normally.
var=hello
prompt='\\\\$var'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Backslash before escaped dollar
script:
# `\\\$` → step 1 produces \$ (Backslash + DollarOrPound). Step 2 keeps
# the literal backslash and the literal $, so the result is `\$`.
prompt='\\\$'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Many backslashes before non-special
script:
# Each `\\` in step 1 produces a literal `\`. Step 2 reduces consecutive
# backslashes pairwise.
prompt='\\\\\\\\X'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt=$'\\\\\\\\\r'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Backslash before newline is line continuation
script:
# `\\\n` produces (Backslash, Newline) → \<LF> in formatted prompt.
# In double-quote escape rules, \<newline> is line continuation and
# consumes both characters.
prompt='\\\n'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

# Same expected behavior when the LF byte is supplied directly.
prompt=$'\\\\\n'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Trailing literal backslash survives
script:
# `\\` at end of prompt should produce a single literal backslash.
prompt='\\'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

# `\\X\\` should produce `\X\`.
prompt='\\X\\'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Backslash followed by working-dir prompt piece
script:
# Make sure prompt pieces whose formatted output happens to contain `\`
# (e.g., AsciiCharacter for octal `\134`) survive intact.
prompt='\134'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

# `\\\w` should yield `\<cwd>`. Use a fixed cwd so brush vs. oracle
# output is deterministic.
cd /
prompt='\\\w'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

name: Bare \$ leaves no protective backslash (issue #1167)
script:
# `\$` alone must format to a bare `$` or `#` — pass 1's protective `\`
# must not leak when the resulting char (e.g. `#` for root) isn't
# double-quote-escapable.
prompt='\$'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

# Same in a context where promptvars would otherwise re-expand a bare $:
var=SHOULD_NOT_APPEAR
prompt='\$var'
shopt -s promptvars
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C
shopt -u promptvars

name: Backslash adjacent to unrecognized escape sequence
script:
# `\\\X` (Backslash + EscapedSequence(\X)) must reduce to a single `\X`.
# An over-eager protective `\` on the EscapedSequence would leak (X
# isn't dq-escapable) and emit `\\X`.
prompt='\\\X'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt='\\\?'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

# X here is dq-escapable, so pass 2 consumes the EscapedSequence's own
# `\` and emits just the literal char.
prompt='\"'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

prompt='\`'
printf '%s' "${prompt@P}" | hexdump -C

cat <>file.txt

echo "This should appear"

non-existent-command 2>&-

name: Redirect for an external command with one file descriptor to spare
script:
ulimit -n 64
# Open files until none are left, then free one, so that opening the
# redirection's target succeeds, but nothing past that can be opened.
fd=10
while [[ $fd -lt 64 ]] && eval "exec $fd</dev/null" 2>/dev/null; do fd=$((fd+1)); done
eval "exec $((fd-1))<&-"
env true 3</dev/null
echo "status: $?"

name: Close output file descriptor
script:
# Open a new output fd (3).
exec 3>test.txt
# Write to the file.
echo "test" >&3
# Close the file.
exec 3>&-
# Make sure we can't write to it.
echo "after close" >&3 || echo "Cannot write to closed fd"

name: Close input file descriptor
script:
# Open an input file descriptor (3).
exec 3<input.txt
# Read from the file.
read line <&3
echo "Read: $line"
# Close the file descriptor.
exec 3<&-
# Make sure we can't read from it.
read line <&3 2>/dev/null || echo "Cannot read from closed fd"

name: Duplicate input file descriptor
script:
# Open an input file descriptor (3).
exec 3<input.txt
# Duplicate it to another descriptor (4).
exec 4<&3
# Read from the new descriptor.
read line <&4
echo "Read: $line"

name: Input file descriptor duplication from stdin
script:
exec 3<&0
echo "test" | { read line <&3; echo "Read: $line"; }

name: Multiple file descriptor redirections
script:
# Open multiple new output fds
exec 3>fd3.txt 4>fd4.txt 5>fd5.txt
# Write to the new fds
echo "fd3" >&3
echo "fd4" >&4
echo "fd5" >&5
# Close the fds
exec 3>&- 4>&- 5>&-
# Read from the files to verify
echo "[3]"
cat fd3.txt
echo "[4]"
fd4.txt
echo "[5]"
fd5.txt

name: High file descriptor numbers
script:

echo "test" 10>fd10.txt >&10
# Dump the file
echo "[10]"
cat fd10.txt

name: Redirection with out-of-range io number falls back to a word
script:

# prefix, so it's treated as an ordinary word argument instead.
echo hi 299999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999>out.txt
cat out.txt

name: Redirection with out-of-range io number duplicated to a valid fd
Redirection with out-of-range io numbers on both sides of a dup
Inheritance of fds from parent
script:
args=""

# NOTE: For now, brush doesn't inherit arbitrary all open fds by default like bash does.
# We need to explicitly specify which fds to inherit.
if [[ $BRUSH_VERSION ]]; then
  args+=" --inherit-fd=3"
fi

$0 $args test.sh 3>output.txt

name: trap runs once for signals that arrive while a program runs

trap 'echo got' USR1
sh -c 'kill -USR1 $PPID; kill -USR1 $PPID; kill -USR1 $PPID; echo child-done'
echo done

name: trap runs for each signal that arrives between commands

kill -USR1 $$

name: trap runs again for its signal arriving during the trap
script:

trap 'n=$((n + 1)); echo "in $n"; [ "$n" -lt 3 ] && kill -USR1 $$; echo "out $n"' USR1
kill -USR1 $$
echo done

script: n=0; trap 'n=$((n + 1)); [ $n -lt 20 ] && kill -USR1 $$' USR1; kill -USR1 $$; echo "n=$n"

sleep 3 &

echo "read=$? x=$x"

echo "read=$? x=$x"

name: SIGPIPE from a builtin's write ends a pipeline stage
script:
i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 3 ]; do printf '%065536d\n' 0; i=$((i + 1)); done | head -n 1 > /dev/null
echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

{ trap 'echo t >> log' PIPE; i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 3 ]; do printf '%0262144d\n' 0; echo "printf=$?" >> log; i=$((i + 1)); done; } 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 > /dev/null
echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
cat log; rm log

{ i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 3 ]; do printf '%0262144d\n' 0; echo "printf=$?" >> log; i=$((i + 1)); done; } 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 > /dev/null
echo "status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
cat log; rm log

name: a signal ignored when a non-interactive shell started can't be trapped
script:

show() {

  local m=$((16#$hex)) out="" s n
  for s in INT QUIT USR1 PIPE TSTP TTIN TTOU; do
    n=$(kill -l "$s"); out+="$s=$(( (m >> (n - 1)) & 1 )) "
  done
  echo "$2: $out"
}
grep SigIgn /proc/self/status > fg.txt; show "$(<fg.txt)" foreground
(grep SigIgn /proc/self/status > sub.txt); show "$(<sub.txt)" subshell

}

show "$(cat <(grep SigIgn /proc/self/status))" procsubst
coproc { grep SigIgn /proc/self/status; }

echo "empty[@]-      : [${empty[@]-DEF}]"

echo "assoc[@]-      : [${assoc[@]-DEF}]"

echo "empty[@]:+     : [${empty[@]:+ALT}]"
echo "empty[@]:-     : [${empty[@]:-DEF}]"

# A non-empty array is set; a single empty element still counts as set.
echo "nonempty[@]+   : [${nonempty[@]+ALT}]"

echo "single[@]+     : [${single[@]+ALT}]"

printf '<%s>' "${@+ALT}" x; echo
printf '<%s>' "${@:+ALT}" x; echo

# Unchanged: [*] still yields one empty word; inside a word nothing is added.
printf '<%s>' "${empty[*]+ALT}" x; echo
printf '<%s>' a"${empty[@]+ALT}"b; echo

script:

mkdir subdir
cd subdir

D=~+
echo "~+: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~-
echo "~-: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

unset OLDPWD
D=~-
echo "~- (without OLDPWD): ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

name: Tilde expansion: dir stack
script:
test_root=$(pwd)

for name in a b c d e f g; do
  mkdir $name
  pushd $name >/dev/null 2>&1
done

D=~2
echo "~2: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~9
echo "~9: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~+2
echo "~+2: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~+9
echo "~+9: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~-2
echo "~-2: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=~-9
echo "~-9: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

name: Tilde expansion: after colons
script:
test_root=~

D=something:~
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=something":"~
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=something:"~"
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=something:~:another:~
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

name: Tilde expansion: unexpanded tildes
script:
test_root=$(pwd)

D="~"
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

D=x~
echo "D: ${D//${test_root}/TEST_ROOT}"

name: Tilde expansion: colon context sensitivity
script:
# Tilde at word start always expands (in both contexts)
echo "echo tilde: $(echo ~)"
var=~
echo "assignment tilde: ${var}"

# Tilde after colon: should NOT expand in non-assignment context
echo "echo with colon: $(echo ~:~/bin)"
echo ~:~/bin

# But SHOULD expand in assignment context
var=~:~/bin
echo "assignment with colon: ${var}"

# Complex PATH-like example
PATH=/usr/bin:~:/bin:~/local
echo "PATH: ${PATH}"

name: Tilde expansion: parameter defaults
script:
echo "Use default value with tilde"
unset myvar
echo "Default: ${myvar:-~}"
echo "myvar after :-: ${myvar}"

echo "Assign default value with tilde"
unset myvar
echo "Assign default: ${myvar:=~}"
echo "myvar after :=: ${myvar}"

echo "Use default with colon-tilde"
unset myvar2
echo "Default colon-tilde: ${myvar2:-~:~/bin}"

echo "Assign default with colon-tilde"
unset myvar3
echo "Assign colon-tilde: ${myvar3:=~:~/bin}"
echo "myvar3 after := ${myvar3}"

name: Tilde expansion: OLDPWD declared without a value
script:
printf "<%s>\n" ~- ~-/x

unset OLDPWD
declare OLDPWD
printf "<%s>\n" ~-

unset OLDPWD
export OLDPWD
printf "<%s>\n" ~-

OLDPWD=
printf "<%s>\n" ~-

name: Tilde expansion: out-of-range dir stack index
script:
# A run of digits too large to fit the dir-stack index type isn't a valid
# index, so the tilde word falls back to (failed) username lookup and is
# left unexpanded, same as an ordinary nonexistent user.
D=~99999999999999999999
echo "D: $D"

D=~-99999999999999999999
echo "D: $D"

D=~+99999999999999999999
echo "D: $D"

name: Tilde expansion in list
script: echo ~/{file.txt,file.txt.bak}

name: Tilde expansion: after the = of an assignment-shaped argument
script:
test_root=~
echo y=~/z | sed "s|${test_root}|ROOT|"
builtin export by=~/z; echo "${by//${test_root}/ROOT}"
command export cz=~/z; echo "${cz//${test_root}/ROOT}"

name: Undefined variables
script:
echo "Undefined: ${undefined}"
echo "Undefined: $undefined"

name: Defined variables
script:
var=xyz
echo "Defined: ${var}"
echo "Defined: var"
echo "Defined: prefix${var}suffix"
echo "Defined: prefix$var"

name: Undefined positional params
script:
echo "Param: $9"
echo "Param: ${9}"

name: High-numbered positional params
script:
echo "Param: $99"
echo "Param: ${99}"

name: Nameref indirect expansion returns target name
script:
target="the_value"
declare -n ref=target
echo "indirect: ${!ref}"
echo "direct: $ref"

name: Nameref with string operations
script:
target="Hello World"
declare -n ref=target
echo "upper: ${ref^^}"
echo "lower: ${ref,,}"
echo "length: ${#ref}"
echo "substring: ${ref:0:5}"
echo "replace: ${ref/World/Bash}"

name: Nameref with default value expansion
script:
declare -n ref=unset_var
echo "default: ${ref:-default_value}"
echo "assign default: ${ref:=assigned}"
echo "unset_var: $unset_var"

name: Nameref with error expansion
script:
declare -n ref=unset_var
echo "${ref:?should error}" 2>/dev/null || echo "caught error"

name: Nameref with alternative expansion
script:
target="exists"
declare -n ref=target
echo "${ref:+alternative}"
unset target
echo "'${ref:+alternative}'"

name: Nameref with pattern removal
script:
target="/usr/local/bin/bash"
declare -n ref=target
echo "## */: ${ref##*/}"
echo "%% /*: ${ref%%/*}"
echo "# */: ${ref#*/}"
echo "% /*: ${ref%/*}"
